1password.description: Password manager for logins, passkeys, secrets and secure sharing.
1password.justification: An encrypted command-line vault built on well-known libraries is doable in a weekend, but that is not what you pay 1Password for. You pay for autofill in the browser and on mobile, passkeys, family or team sharing, account recovery and leak monitoring. In security, doing it badly is worse than not doing it. Bitwarden (free) or KeePassXC are, for almost everyone, the best replacement.
perdez: Autofill in the browser and on mobile.
alternatives: Free plan with unlimited passwords, passkeys, secure notes and sharing with one person; built-in TOTP and full reports are paid.
Bitwarden-compatible server to host yourself; managing recovery is on you.
Mature local password manager, with a database file that you keep yourself.
1password.prompt:
Build me a local, encrypted password vault, command line first, to replace 1Password. It does not fill in forms.

Stack: a single Go binary, with filippo.io/age for encryption and Argon2id (golang.org/x/crypto) to derive the key from my passphrase. Use these libraries exactly as documented, without inventing any cryptography.

To do:
- A single encrypted file ~/.vault/vault.age containing JSON entries: name, username, password, URL, notes, update date.
- Commands: add, get <name> (copies to the clipboard and clears it after 20 seconds), ls, gen (random 32-character password), edit, rm.
- Fuzzy search on the name for `get`; never display a password on screen without --show.
- `vault backup` writes a dated encrypted copy to a folder defined in .env: already encrypted, it can be synced by any storage.
- Import from a 1Password CSV export to migrate in one command.
- Everything local: no server, no accounts, no telemetry.

Out of scope: autofill, passkeys, sharing. If I need them, the honest solution is KeePassXC or Bitwarden: say so as is in the README.

README: a five-line threat model, how the key derivation works, and a clear warning: losing the passphrase means losing everything.

5stelle.description: Cloud hotel management software to track bookings, invoices and arrivals.
5stelle.justification: A cloud PMS handles arrivals, invoicing and bookings while rooms are being sold in parallel on other channels: a sync error means a room sold twice. A dashboard or arrival emails can be built around 5stelle; the core of the PMS cannot.
alternatives: Open-source hotel PMS and booking engine (PHP, OSL-3.0 licence), self-hostable, active repository.
Free PMS (GPL-3.0) for small hotels and guesthouses, German and English interface, active repository.
Free PMS with no room limit (planning, bookings, invoicing), in French; paid channel manager from €25/month.
Spanish vendor with a free PMS version (reservations, calendar, invoicing); channel manager as a paid option.
French PMS for hotels and restaurants with built-in channel manager, 45-day free trial.

adobe-creative-cloud.description: Adobe's suite of creative software (Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere Pro, Lightroom…) by subscription. Creative Cloud Pro at €78.65 a month with annual commitment (price including tax, read on the site).
adobe-creative-cloud.justification: Photoshop, Illustrator or Premiere are professional software of several million lines of code, with file formats that the whole industry uses. No in-house development replaces them. For occasional use (simple retouching, a logo), free alternatives exist; for professional use, keep the suite.
perdez: The PSD, AI and PRPROJ file formats exchanged across the profession
Professional-grade retouching, vector and editing tools

agendrix.description: Scheduling, time clocking and availability software for restaurant and hotel teams.
agendrix.justification: Scheduling, time clocking and availability can be rebuilt fairly quickly. What you lose is the tracking of labour law: overtime, rest between shifts, export to payroll, which change with the law and the collective agreement. Agendrix is a good example of what can be built in-house for the schedule, but not for the legal count.
perdez: The proven mobile app with notifications.
alternatives: Free time tracking (AGPL-3.0), self-hostable, with a clock-in/clock-out mode; does not handle scheduling.
Free restaurant schedules up to 10 employees, paid version from €9.90 excl. VAT/month; French vendor.
agendrix.prompt:
Build me a scheduling, time-clocking and availability tool, for my venue, to replace a subscription.

Stack: web app (Next.js or Node/Express) with SQLite, hosted on my small server, usable on phone and computer. No mandatory paid service, no telemetry.

Core of the tool:
- Schedule per position with weekly templates.
- Availability declared by employees, shift swaps approved by the manager.
- Time clocking from phone or a tablet at the entrance, with the gap between planned and actual hours.

Requirements:
- Weekly schedule by position and by shift, with drag and drop, copy of the previous week and publication to the teams.
- Availability and leave requests entered by the employee, approved by the manager.
- Configurable alerts: 11 h rest between two shifts, 10 h of work per day, weekly working time. Default values from the French Labour Code, to be adapted to the HCR collective agreement by my accountant.
- CSV export of hours per employee and per period, for my accountant.
- Employee data: role-based access (manager, employee), password or magic link, change log.

Out of scope: payroll, DSN and geolocation of clocking.

README: installation, backup, and a reminder that this tool is not payroll software and calculates no salary, no DSN, no DPAE, and that legal counts remain to be checked by my accountant.

agicap.description: French cash-flow management and forecasting platform for small and medium businesses: bank account centralisation, forecasts, automatic reconciliation and categorisation.
agicap.justification: A cash-flow forecast built from CSV exports of the bank (expected receipts and payments, projected balance) is easy to build. What you lose: the automatic connection to banks, categorisation and integrations with accounting software. For a small business with a single bank, replaceable; for several accounts, keep the tool.
agicap.prompt:
Build me a cash-flow forecasting tool for a small business, without claiming to replace Agicap or do official accounting.

Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, SQLite. Data at my place, secrets in .env, no telemetry.

To do:
- Import of CSV statements that I export myself from my bank, with duplicate detection.
- Categorisation of entries by rules I define, and manual correction.
- Expected receipts and payments (customer invoices to collect, recurring costs), with date and amount.
- Projected balance curve over 3, 6 and 12 months, with an alert if the balance falls below a threshold I set.
- Simple scenarios: what if a big customer pays 30 days late?
- CSV export; single user; tests on the projected balance calculation; README with the limits.

Out of scope: live bank connection, automatic reconciliation, accounting. Never state that the figures are accounting-accurate.
alternatives: Budgeting and account tracking software (MIT), self-hostable; no business cash flow forecasting.
Self-hosted personal finance manager (AGPL): accounts, budgets, categories and rules.
Web interface for plain-text double-entry accounting with Beancount (MIT), for people who like to keep numbers under control.

agorapulse.description: Social media management: publishing, unified inbox, listening, reports and return-on-investment tracking.
agorapulse.justification: Writing, previewing and scheduling posts, you can do. What is not in your hands are the connections to the networks: their APIs change, some are paid or subject to approval, and a post that fails silently is worse than no tool. At €99 a month per user, Agorapulse also sells the unified inbox, listening and reports. Replaceable only if you publish on one or two open networks.
perdez: Publishing reliability when the networks' APIs change.
Team approval workflows and the content library.
alternatives: Free social media scheduling and publishing platform.
Self-hosted social media management software, more modest than Agorapulse.
agorapulse.prompt:
Build me a personal social post scheduler, a modest version of Agorapulse. It does not replace the unified inbox or the statistics.

Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, BullMQ.

To do:
- Drafts, per-platform preview (character and media limits), calendar and publishing queue.
- Single user, private, with import and export so I am not locked in.
- Publishing through the official API of one or two open networks (Mastodon, Bluesky), with retries and a clear failure state.
- Sample data clearly labelled and easy to delete.
- Empty, loading, error and success states; keyboard navigation and decent contrast.
- Secrets in .env, no telemetry, targeted tests and one end-to-end test, README with the limits.

Out of scope: reliable publishing on every network, statistics history and attribution. Do not simulate any integration.

ahrefs.description: SEO platform built on very large web databases: backlinks, keywords, results pages and AI search.
ahrefs.justification: Tracking your own keywords and auditing your site is a weekend, for a few euros of API. But Ahrefs sells an index of the web that it crawled itself: backlinks, keywords, history of results. No solo project reproduces it, and scraping Google directly leads to being blocked. Your tool replaces the dashboard, not the data.
perdez: The scale and freshness of the data.
ahrefs.prompt:
Build me a daily rank tracker and a site auditor for my own domain, the only part of Ahrefs worth building solo.

Stack: Python, httpx, SQLite, Flask and Chart.js for a local dashboard.

To do:
- My keywords are in keywords.txt (up to 50). Fetch positions through a search results API (Serper.dev or SerpAPI, key in .env; the free plans are enough). Do not scrape Google directly: it ends up blocked.
- Store keyword, position, ranked URL and date in SQLite, run daily by cron.
- Dashboard on localhost: one curve per keyword and the list of the week's biggest movements.
- An audit crawler for my domain: broken links, missing or duplicate titles and descriptions, redirect chains, pages under 200 words; results in audit.md.
- Clicks and impressions per query through the Google Search Console API, displayed next to the positions.
- Everything local, with no accounts or telemetry.

Out of scope: backlinks, keyword volume and difficulty, competitor analysis. Do not try to simulate them by scraping; that dataset is the subscription.

README: API keys, Search Console connection steps (allow an hour for OAuth in Google Cloud), and a reminder that Ahrefs is a proprietary index of the web.

airkitchen.description: NF525 touchscreen till for restaurants and food businesses, including hotels and campsites.
airkitchen.justification: In France, till software must be NF525-certified or covered by a certificate of compliance (article 286 of the French tax code): an in-house till has neither, with a fine of €7,500 per non-compliant system. AirKitchen is a touchscreen till for restaurants and food businesses, including hotels and campsites: takings, receipts and closings must remain tamper-proof. Go with the vendor; keep custom work for the extras (menu, reservations).
alternatives: Open-source ERP (LGPL) whose Point of Sale app handles floor plan, kitchen and QR code. NF525 certification not confirmed for the Community edition: check with the vendor before using it as a till in France.
French NF525-certified till with floor plan and kitchen screen, free up to 100 receipts a month.
NF525-certified online cash register, free with paid options, restaurant version.

airtable.description: Spreadsheet-style database, with forms, views, automations and interfaces for teams.
airtable.justification: A spreadsheet-style database with typed fields, linked tables, saved views and CSV import/export is doable in a few days for solo use, and Baserow or Teable exist as free software. Airtable weighs mostly on teamwork: permissions per table, automations, interfaces for non-technical people, syncs. If you are alone, replaceable. As soon as colleagues join in, that is where the subscription is justified.
perdez: The mobile app, access rights and scaling up.
alternatives: Open-source no-code database (MIT licence), with a hosted free plan limited to 3,000 rows and a smaller ecosystem of integrations.
Spreadsheet-style database under the AGPL-3.0 licence, with a hosted free plan, less mature than Airtable on integrations and interfaces.
Grid with forms, automations and scripts, whose free plan allows up to 10,000 rows.
Relational database tool less like a spreadsheet, with forms, views and automations on the free plan.
The same product in a free version, limited to five editors and 1,000 records per base.
airtable.prompt:
Build me a personal spreadsheet-style database to replace Airtable.

Stack: Node, Express, better-sqlite3 (one file data/base.db), Tabulator grid with plain JavaScript, no build step.

To do:
- Create tables and columns from the interface, typed text, number, date, choice, checkbox or URL. Each table is a real SQLite table, which other tools can query.
- Inline editing in the grid, sorting on click, filters per column.
- Saved views (name, filters, sort, hidden columns) listed in a sidebar.
- Link columns: a cell references rows from another table, chosen from a list, shown as clickable pills.
- A quick entry page /form/<table> with one field per column.
- CSV import and export per table.
- Localhost only, no account or telemetry.

Out of scope: multi-user permissions, automations, hosted interfaces. When colleagues need to enter data, that is the moment to use Airtable.

README: installation and location of the database.

alan.description: French health insurance (mutual insurer) for companies and individuals, with a mobile app, fast reimbursements and prevention services.
alan.justification: Alan is an insurer: it carries the risk, reimburses care and answers to regulation that no in-house tool covers. You can write a mutual-insurer comparison page or a reimbursement tracking sheet, but you cannot do without the insurer.
perdez: The mobile app and prevention services
Administrative management on the company side

amenitiz.description: Management suite for independent hotels, with PMS, booking engine and channel management.
amenitiz.justification: Amenitiz bundles PMS, booking engine, channel manager and payments in a single subscription, with no commission on direct bookings; its built-in payment, AmenitizPay, charges 1.5% + €0.25 per transaction. It targets small hotels without an IT person: the value is in the whole package already wired to the booking platforms. A direct-booking site can be built; the PMS and distribution stay with the vendor.
alternatives: Open-source hotel PMS and booking engine (PHP, OSL-3.0 licence), self-hostable, active repository.
Free PMS with no room limit (planning, bookings, invoicing), in French; paid channel manager from €25/month.
Spanish vendor with a free PMS version (reservations, calendar, invoicing); channel manager as a paid option.
PMS and channel manager priced per unit, from €15.50/month, no commission on bookings.
French PMS for hotels and restaurants with built-in channel manager, 45-day free trial.

apaleo.description: Open German hotel PMS (Apaleo GmbH), built around APIs: reservations, invoicing, payments (Apaleo Pay) and an integration marketplace, for hotels and holiday residences.
apaleo.justification: A PMS touches invoicing, payments and syncing availability with sales channels: an error can cost a room sold twice. Apaleo is a special case, because its open API lets you build tools around it (dashboard, arrival emails) without redoing the core. The core itself cannot be rebuilt: keep the PMS and customise around it.
perdez: Reliable syncing of rooms with sales channels
alternatives: Open-source hotel PMS and booking engine (PHP, OSL-3.0 licence), self-hostable, active repository.

apicbase.description: Recipe, purchasing, stock and menu management for restaurant groups and central kitchens.
apicbase.justification: Designed for central kitchens and multi-site groups, consolidating data at this scale goes well beyond an in-house development project.
alternatives: Recipe cards, stock, inventories and supplier orders for kitchens, modules from €49 excl. VAT/month, free trial.
French vendor of recipe cards, stock and margin tracking for restaurants, from €80/month, 14-day trial.
HACCP, stock, recipes and supplier orders suite for restaurants, from €19.90 excl. VAT/month, limited free plan.

ariane-systems.description: Kiosks and online check-in to automate guest arrival and departure at hotels.
ariane-systems.justification: Ariane Systems supplies check-in kiosks and online check-in so guests can arrive and leave without going through reception. The kiosk software is only one part: there is also the hardware, the payment, the link with the PMS and handing over a key or an access code. It is an integration project, not an app to develop.

asana.description: Team project management: projects, tasks, owners, dependencies and progress updates.
asana.justification: Project tracking for a small team, with tasks, owners, simple dependencies and comments, is a few days of work, and free tools (Plane, OpenProject) already do it. Asana weighs elsewhere: its integrations, automations, cross-team reports and the trust of an organisation that has worked in it for years. For a team of 3, replaceable. For 30 people with established habits, the cost of switching exceeds the saving.
alternatives: Work tracking in the spirit of Linear and Jira, self-hostable; the deployment relies on several services.
Complete project management suite for formal project plans; the interface is dense and no-code automation is limited.
JetBrains project tracker, free up to ten users, aimed at development teams.
Project management suite for small teams, which also covers goals and time tracking.
Project tracking, timesheets, Gantt charts and wiki, highly configurable but to install and administer yourself.
asana.prompt:
Build me a project tracking tool for a small team, to replace Asana.

Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind, PostgreSQL with Drizzle, Docker Compose.

To do:
- Organisations, projects, members, issues with labels, cycles and milestones.
- List, kanban and simple timeline views, on a single issue model; dependencies between issues.
- Comments, mentions, assignments, watchers, progress updates, full activity log.
- Owner, member and viewer roles, with a test for each change.
- Search, CSV import and export, email notifications, daily backups.
- Local launch in one command, sample data, health checks, migrations, administrator recovery command.
- Secrets in .env, no telemetry, tests, README.

Out of scope: hundreds of integrations, enterprise portfolio planning, SSO, native mobile apps.

asterio.description: Cloud PMS for hotels, restaurants and spas, with multi-activity management and built-in point of sale.
asterio.justification: Asterio brings accommodation, dining and spa into a single PMS, with an integrated point of sale. The hard part is not the screen but cross-billing (one bill mixing room, meals and treatments) and payment collection: an integrated till has to follow French rules on cash-register software, with a certificate or an attestation from the vendor. An in-house tool ticks neither box.
alternatives: Open-source hotel PMS and booking engine (PHP, OSL-3.0 licence), self-hostable, active repository.
Free PMS (GPL-3.0) for small hotels and guesthouses, German and English interface, active repository.
French PMS for hotels and restaurants with built-in channel manager, 45-day free trial.
French PMS for small hotels and guesthouses, installed locally, 60-day trial, version certified for France.
PMS and channel manager priced per unit, from €15.50/month, no commission on bookings.

axonaut.description: All-in-one French management software (Labège): CRM, quotes, invoicing, cash flow, expense claims, stock, with business account and electronic invoicing.
axonaut.justification: The CRM, quotes and invoices can be rebuilt; they are forms and PDFs. Bank-linked cash flow, accounting and electronic invoicing, on the other hand, need connections and a tracking of rules that the vendor provides. For simple sales use, replaceable; for full management with the accountant, keep the tool.
perdez: The built-in business account and cards
Connections to more than 14,000 tools claimed by the vendor
alternatives: Free management suite: customers, quotes, invoices, calendar and payment tracking, developed in France.
Free ERP combining CRM, quotes, invoicing and project tracking; heavier to set up.
Modular self-hostable ERP and CRM (free community edition): sales, invoicing, inventory, HR.
axonaut.prompt:
Build me a small sales management tool for a freelancer or very small business, without claiming to replace Axonaut or do official accounting.

Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, SQLite. Data at my place, secrets in .env, no telemetry.

To do:
- Customers and prospects: record, history of exchanges, sales follow-up stage (new, quote sent, won, lost).
- Quote then invoice from the quote, as PDF: continuous numbering with no gaps, mandatory mentions, VAT per line, deposit and balance.
- Invoices are never deleted or edited: a mistake is corrected with a credit note.
- Payment tracking and reminder by email (configurable SMTP).
- Expense claims: entry with photo of the receipt, approval status.
- CSV export of customers and invoices for my accountant; simple backup.
- Tests on numbering and totals; README with the limits.

Out of scope: accounting, bank reconciliation, VAT returns, and the transmission of invoices through an approved platform that electronic invoicing reform will eventually require (timetable to be checked). Never state that the documents comply with that reform.

bear.description: Markdown note-taking app for Mac, iPhone and iPad. Free version with local notes; Bear Pro adds iCloud sync, themes and extra exports.
bear.justification: A Markdown notes app with tags, search and export is a very accessible project. What Bear brings is the care of the Apple interface and iCloud sync. If you want notes on all your devices, an installable web app is enough, and you keep your files. To check: offline writing.
perdez: The polished interface on Mac, iPhone and iPad
Text search in PDFs and images (OCR)
alternatives: Free note-taking (AGPL-3.0) in local files, with links between notes and a daily journal.
End-to-end encrypted note-taking app (GPL-3.0), with sync and a self-hosting option.
Block-based knowledge management, self-hostable (AGPL), with links between notes and sync.
bear.prompt:
Build me a simple Markdown notes app, on all my devices, to replace Bear.

Stack: installable web app (PWA), Node or Next.js, SQLite.

To do:
- Markdown editor with preview; notes with nested tags (#project/idea) created by typing the #.
- Fast full-text search, pinned notes, trash with restore.
- Works offline (service worker) and syncs on reconnection without losing a note.
- Export of one note or all as Markdown, PDF and HTML.
- Simple authentication, daily backup; tests on sync; README with the limits.

Out of scope: text recognition in images, collaborative sharing.

billiv.description: Digital receipt turned into a loyalty programme and Google review collection.
billiv.justification: Digitising the receipt and attaching a points programme is a reasonable project; integration with the existing till is what takes the most care.
perdez: Direct integration with your till, which generates the receipt.
The customer app already installed on your customers' phones, if any.
alternatives: Digital stamp loyalty card with a free plan and no limit on customers, Pro version at €12/month.
Free digital loyalty card (Apple/Google Wallet), Google review wheel as a paid option from €18 excl. VAT/month.
billiv.prompt:
Build me a digital receipt with loyalty and review collection, for my venue, to replace a subscription.

Stack: web app (Next.js or Node/Express) with SQLite, hosted on my small server, usable on phone and computer. No mandatory paid service, no telemetry.

Core of the tool:
- Digital receipt sent by email or accessible by QR code after payment, with the bill's detail.
- Simple loyalty programme: one point per euro or one stamp per visit, configurable reward.
- Invitation to leave a Google review, sent to all customers who consented.

Requirements:
- GDPR: explicit consent at collection (unticked box, clear wording), unsubscribe link in every message, export and deletion of a customer on request, configurable retention period.
- Honest reviews: every customer receives the same invitation, with no prior sorting by satisfaction, and no reward is tied to a positive review. The review platforms' rules apply.
- Emails sent through a configurable SMTP server, with rate limiting; no scraping of the review platforms.
- Simple dashboard: invitations sent, clicks, evolution over time.

Out of scope: integration with the till (the bill is entered or imported as CSV); this digital receipt does not replace the certified till's receipt.

README: installation, SMTP configuration, GDPR reminder (purposes, legal basis, retention) and a reminder that links to the review platforms are entered by hand.

bitwarden.description: Open-source password manager, offered as a hosted service or to install yourself.
bitwarden.justification: Here you rebuild nothing: you install Vaultwarden, a free server compatible with Bitwarden's apps, on a small server. Half a day is enough. The real cost is elsewhere: you become responsible for backups, security updates and the availability of your passwords. If that worries you, stay on the free or Premium plan.
perdez: Emergency access and family or team sharing, depending on the plan.
Peace of mind: no one but you fixes the vulnerabilities.
alternatives: Unofficial server compatible with Bitwarden clients, to host yourself; backups, updates and outages become your business.
Vault stored as an encrypted local file, with good autofill; syncing and sharing are up to you.
Bitwarden's free plan: unlimited items, devices and passkeys; without built-in TOTP, attachments or emergency access.
Team-oriented password manager with sharing; needs a server, a database and OpenPGP key management.
Vault for passwords, passkeys and disposable email addresses, with a self-hosting option.
bitwarden.prompt:
Set up a self-hosted password vault to replace Bitwarden Premium.

Do not develop a password manager: deploy Vaultwarden, the server compatible with Bitwarden clients, on my VPS.

To do:
- A docker-compose.yml with the vaultwarden/server image and a data volume in ./vw-data.
- Caddy in front, for automatic HTTPS on a subdomain that I give you (the apps require it).
- Once my account is created, close sign-ups (SIGNUPS_ALLOWED=false), put the admin token in .env, expose nothing else.
- Use the official Bitwarden apps and extensions, pointed at my server: autofill, mobile and passkeys keep working.
- A nightly backup: archive of vw-data, encrypted with age, copied off the server. Write restore.sh and make me run a restore test before I rely on it.
- Import my current vault through Bitwarden's standard export/import.

Out of scope: emergency access, organisation or family sharing.

README: launch, account creation, update procedure, restore test. State clearly that clients keep the vault cached (a down server does not lock me out), but that I am now solely responsible for security updates.

biver-io.description: French software for group bookings and private hire for restaurants, bars, brasseries and reception halls: online form, planning and CRM.
biver-io.justification: A request form on your site, a shared calendar and a contact list cover most of private hire: that is the tool's scope, and it can be rebuilt without difficulty. What you lose: the form already integrated into your site, the calendar and CRM fed automatically by each request, and a free 14-day trial to compare before you commit.
perdez: The form already built in, ready to copy.
alternatives: Open-source ERP/CRM (GPL) for quotes, invoices, customers and calendar, developed in France.
Free French invoicing software: unlimited quotes, invoices and customers.
biver-io.prompt:
Build me a group reservation and private-hire tool, for my venue, to replace a subscription.

Stack: web app (Next.js or Node/Express) with SQLite, hosted on my small server, usable on phone and computer. No mandatory paid service, no telemetry.

Core of the tool:
- Private-hire request form embeddable in my site, with room availability.
- Event calendar and a contact record created with each request.
- Automatic follow-ups for quotes with no reply.

Requirements:
- Online request form (date, number of people, type of event, budget, contact) that creates a record in a tracking board: new, quote sent, accepted, deposit received, done.
- Quote then invoice as PDF: continuous numbering with no gaps, mandatory mentions, VAT per line, deposit. To be validated by my accountant.
- Function sheet as PDF to brief the teams (times, menu, floor plan, contacts).
- Event calendar with room-conflict detection.

Out of scope: online payment.

README: installation, backup, and a reminder that the tool produces documents but does not replace the approved platform that electronic invoicing reform will eventually require, which remains out of scope.

booking-com-extranet.description: Extranet to manage listings, rates and availability on the number-one OTA for French hotels.
booking-com-extranet.justification: The Booking.com extranet is the free tool through which a hotel manages its listings, rates and availability; Booking is paid through a commission on each reservation. What has value is the platform's audience, which no in-house tool can reproduce. If you sell on several platforms, a channel manager saves you from updating each extranet by hand.

booking-shake.description: French software to manage groups and events: requests, quotes, invoices, schedules and function sheets, for hotels, restaurant-bars and event venues.
booking-shake.justification: The core (request form, quote, invoice, event schedule) can be built with a form, a spreadsheet or simple database and a PDF generator. What you lose: the Stripe payment links already hooked up, syncing of function sheets with the teams and compliance with electronic invoicing, which changes invoice-issuing obligations in France. For the occasional private hire a home-made solution is enough; for a regular volume of events, the tool is justified.
perdez: Payment links that are already built in.
Syncing function sheets with the teams.
alternatives: Open-source ERP/CRM (GPL) for quotes, invoices, customers and calendar, developed in France.
Free French invoicing software: unlimited quotes, invoices and customers.
booking-shake.prompt:
Build me a group and event management tool, for my venue, to replace a subscription.

Stack: web app (Next.js or Node/Express) with SQLite, hosted on my small server, usable on phone and computer. No mandatory paid service, no telemetry.

Core of the tool:
- Centralising requests (form, email entered by hand) with status.
- Quote, invoice, deposit with a Stripe payment link in test mode to start with.
- Event schedule and function sheet as PDF.

Requirements:
- Online request form (date, number of people, type of event, budget, contact) that creates a record in a tracking board: new, quote sent, accepted, deposit received, done.
- Quote then invoice as PDF: continuous numbering with no gaps, mandatory mentions, VAT per line, deposit. To be validated by my accountant.
- Function sheet as PDF to brief the teams (times, menu, floor plan, contacts).
- Event calendar with room-conflict detection.

Out of scope: syncing with a PMS and compliance with electronic invoicing.

README: installation, backup, and a reminder that the tool produces documents but does not replace the approved platform that electronic invoicing reform will eventually require, which remains out of scope.

brevo.description: Email sending platform for newsletters and transactional messages, with CRM and automations.
brevo.justification: Collecting subscribers with proof of consent, sending a low-volume newsletter and publishing an archive is a few days with Amazon SES. Brevo, a French vendor, is paid for mainly for deliverability, the CRM, SMS and automations bundle, and turnkey compliance. The GDPR requires provable consent and easy unsubscribing: doable, but it is up to you to keep it up. For a few hundred subscribers, replaceable; for sends that keep your business alive, keep a provider.
perdez: The deliverability and experience of people who do this for a living.
Support and compliance handled for you.

To do:

- A single encrypted file ~/.vault/store.age, encrypted with the age tool (calling the command-line binary) from a passphrase requested each time and never written to disk.
- Each entry: name, username, password, URL, notes, update date. All as JSON inside the encrypted file, decrypted only in memory.
- `vault gen`: random 24-character password via crypto.randomBytes, with an option for a 4-word passphrase (diceware).
- `vault backup`: dated encrypted copy in ~/.vault/backups/, which I will sync with the tool of my choice.
- 100% local: no account, no telemetry, no network call.

Out of scope: autofill, passkeys, leak alerts, sharing. Do not invent any cryptography: use age as is.

A mistake in a return is costly, and the law changes. A home-made tool is a logbook, not an accountant.
perdez: Updates to tax and accounting rules.
Preparing and tracking tax and social returns.
Security and disaster recovery verified by audits.
alternatives: Free ERP combining CRM, quotes, contracts, projects, time tracking and invoicing; much heavier to set up than Indy.
Practical management suite covering quotes, contracts, tasks, time and invoicing.
indy.prompt:
Build me the most honest tool possible to track my freelance income and expenses, without claiming to replace Indy or do official accounting.

Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, SQLite.

To do:
- Import of CSV statements that I export myself from my bank, with duplicate detection.
- Categorisation of entries by rules I define, and manual correction.
- Reconciliation of balances and totals per month and per category.
- A register exportable as CSV for my accountant.
- Single user, local data, secrets in .env, no telemetry.
- Sample data clearly labelled and easy to delete; tests on the totals calculation; README with the limits.

Out of scope: live bank connection, tax and social rules, preparation of returns. Never state that the figures are compliant.

innovorder.description: Ordering kiosks and till for fast food.
innovorder.justification: Touch kiosks, a certified till and multiple integrations (delivery, kitchen) form a hardware-plus-software package too heavy for a small business to rebuild.
alternatives: Open-source ERP (LGPL) whose Point of Sale app handles floor plan, kitchen and QR code. NF525 certification not confirmed for the Community edition: check with the vendor before using it as a till in France.
Self-hosted restaurant till and ordering (AGPL): QR menu, tables, reservations, kitchen screen. No NF525 certification announced: check before using it as a till in France.

inpulse.description: Artificial-intelligence sales forecasts at ingredient level, inventories and supplier orders.
inpulse.justification: An AI forecasting engine trained on sales history is data engineering well beyond a conventional stock management tool.

intercom.description: Customer service platform: website messaging, shared inbox, knowledge base and AI agent.
intercom.justification: A chat widget on your site, a shared inbox and a small help base can be self-hosted in a few days, and Chatwoot is free and mature. Intercom, for its part, sells the AI agent that resolves requests on its own, product tours, targeted messaging and large-scale support operations. To answer your visitors from a single inbox, replaceable. To automate support for a high-volume product, no.
perdez: The AI agent that handles some requests on its own.
Integrations with the team's other tools.
alternatives: Open-source (MIT licence) support inbox with chat, email and help centre, less rich than Intercom for proactive messages and AI.
Open-source live chat tool (Apache-2.0) with routing, transcripts and canned replies, with a slightly dated interface.
Open-source ticketing system (AGPL-3.0) with email, chat, SLAs and knowledge base, heavier to install.
Free live chat, tickets and knowledge base, with the tawk.to notice shown on the free widget.
Free hosted ticketing for unlimited users, as long as Helpdesk is your only free Odoo app.
intercom.prompt:
Build me an inbox for my website and a help base, to replace the simple part of Intercom.

Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL with Drizzle, WebSockets, Docker Compose.

To do:
- A chat widget for websites: reconnection, unread counter, file limits, availability status.
- A shared inbox with filters, alert when two agents open the same conversation, internal notes, canned replies, searchable history.
- A public knowledge base with search.
- Email and in-browser notifications; immutable log of assignments and status changes.
- Anti-spam, configurable retention period, export and deletion of a contact (GDPR).
- Docker Compose, backups, health checks, migrations, administrator recovery procedure.
- Secrets in .env, no telemetry, tests, README.

Out of scope: multiple social channels, AI agent trained on support data, agent scheduling, SSO and enterprise compliance.

iqoo.description: Temperature control, traceability and simplified management of the food safety plan.
iqoo.justification: Regulation (EC) 852/2004 requires food businesses to have a food safety plan based on HACCP principles, whose records (temperatures, cleaning, receiving) justify that the procedures are applied. The texts consulted set no format (paper or digital) for these records: what matters is that they are reliable and kept. Temperature control and traceability are a textbook case for the digital form. The basic plan is free: the saving is small, and the point of a custom build is to fit your own documents and thresholds exactly. Watch the timestamps and history: that is what gives a reading its evidential value.
perdez: The free entry plan, with no development effort.
The alerts for threshold overruns that are already battle-tested.
Pro and Enterprise plans for several sites.
alternatives: French HACCP software with a free plan (manual temperatures, receiving, traceability); Pro at €49.90 excl. VAT/month with scheduling.
Web and mobile HACCP app with a free starter plan of 4 modules (including temperature readings).
HACCP: temperatures, cleaning plan and traceability, from €47 excl. VAT/month billed annually, no commitment.
iqoo.prompt:
Build me a temperature control tool with overrun alerts, for my restaurant, to replace a HACCP subscription.

Stack: installable phone web app (PWA, mobile first), Node, Express, SQLite (better-sqlite3), hosted on my small server. No heavy front-end framework.

Core of the tool:
- Configurable zones and equipment (positive cold room, negative, display case, hot dishes) with minimum and maximum thresholds.
- Entering a reading in two taps; if the value goes outside the threshold, the non-conformity opens automatically.
- Notification (email or ntfy) when a reading is out of range or missing.
- Trend chart per piece of equipment over 7 days.

Common requirements (a reading only counts as evidence if it is reliable):
- Every record is timestamped by the server, with the user. A reading is never edited or erased: a correction creates a new line that points back to the old one (append-only log).
- Deviations (temperature out of range, cleaning not done) trigger a non-conformity to handle: cause, corrective action, closing date.
- Thresholds, zones (cold rooms, hot dishes) and checklists are set in a configuration file, without touching the code.
- PDF export per period, ready to show during a health inspection. Configurable data retention period.
- Several users (PIN code per employee), no email account. No telemetry.
- Simple traceability: products in with batch and use-by date, out into production.

Out of scope: connected probes, several venues, certification.

README: installation, database backup, and a reminder that this tool documents your food safety plan but does not replace it: have it reviewed by your inspection body or a hygiene consultant.

jotform.description: Online form builder with payments, approval workflows, tables, PDFs and apps.
jotform.justification: A basic form (fields, validation, email sending, CSV export) can be built in a weekend, and Tally or OpnForm already do it. Jotform plays in another category: a huge widget catalogue, built-in payments, PDF generation, approval workflows and compliance options. If you only use fields and emails, replaceable. If you take payments or get things signed, keep it.
jotform.prompt:
Build me a personal form builder to replace Jotform.

Stack: Node, Express, better-sqlite3. Two surfaces: an administration reachable on localhost only, and public pages /f/<slug> for anyone with the link.

To do:
- Forms are stored as JSON in SQLite. Fields: text, email, long text, choice, checkbox, date and file upload (uploads/ folder, 10 MB maximum).
- Server-side validation of required fields and email format, thank-you message per form, honeypot field and per-IP rate limit.
- Each submission is recorded with the timestamp and the form version. On the admin side: a table per form with CSV export.
- A plain-text summary email for each response (SMTP in .env).
- Only the public pages are exposed; no accounts, no telemetry.

Out of scope: payments, PDF generation, approval workflows, widget catalogue.

README: placing the public part behind a reverse proxy, location of uploaded files.
alternatives: Open-source form builder (AGPL), self-hostable.
Open-source conversational form builder (AGPL).
Free form builder with unlimited forms and responses.

just-eat-pro.description: Meal delivery marketplace; its extranet lets restaurateurs manage orders and menus.
just-eat-pro.justification: Just Eat Pro is the extranet to manage orders and menus on the Just Eat marketplace. What matters to a restaurateur is that the platform's customers see their menu. Replacing the extranet with an in-house tool brings back no orders. The lever is elsewhere: promoting your own direct ordering.

ke-booking.description: Hotel SaaS software combining scheduling, booking engine and channel manager.
ke-booking.justification: KE-booking combines scheduling, booking engine and channel manager. The risk is double booking: if a channel is not updated in time, the room is sold twice. A home-made tool would therefore have to guarantee permanent sync with every platform, which only a specialist vendor maintains.
alternatives: Open-source hotel PMS (OSL-3.0) with booking engine and website, self-hosted.
Cloud PMS, booking engine and channel manager billed by usage from €15.50/month, no commitment.
French PMS for independent hotels, from €65 excl. VAT/month for 10 rooms, no commission.

klaviyo.description: Email and SMS platform for online commerce, plugged into the shop's customer data.
klaviyo.justification: The emailing interface can be copied; what makes Klaviyo is the shop data linked in real time, segmentation, abandoned-basket automations and, above all, a sender reputation built on billions of sends. A home-made tool does not reproduce that responsibly. At the scale of a small shop with a modest list, a free tool like listmonk with a sending provider is enough. Beyond that, no.
perdez: Segmentation and automatic scenarios (abandoned basket, follow-up).
alternatives: Self-hosted newsletter and mailing-list manager, very performant.
Open-source marketing automation platform.
klaviyo.prompt:
Build me the most honest tool possible to send marketing emails to my online-shop customers, without claiming to replace Klaviyo.

Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL. Sending only through a reputable email provider that I choose.

To do:
- A subscriber database with CSV import and export, timestamped consent, one-click unsubscribe and suppression list.
- A simple email editor that exports clean HTML, with preview and text version.
- Batch sending through the provider, with rate limits and resume after failure, and handling of bounce and complaint webhooks.
- A demonstration page with sample data clearly labelled and easy to delete.
- Private single-user mode, secrets in .env, no telemetry.
- Targeted tests, one end-to-end test, README with installation, backup and limits.

Deliberately excluded: segmentation and automation at scale, payments, recommendations, audience network, SMS. Do not simulate any integration.

klixi.description: All-round marketing toolbox: website creation, social media management and customer loyalty.
klixi.justification: Three different tools (website, social media, loyalty) brought together in one suite: far too broad to be rebuilt and maintained by a single business.
alternatives: Social media post scheduling, open source (AGPL), self-hostable. Covers only the social media side.
Free Google Business Profile: opening hours, posts and replies to customer reviews.
Online ordering with no commission, free Starter plan (20 orders/month), hosted in France.

komia.description: All-in-one platform for staff scheduling, time clocking and HACCP compliance.
komia.justification: Scheduling and time clocking can reasonably be rebuilt; the HACCP module is simple in itself, but making the two coexist in a single reliable tool takes more work than it looks.
perdez: HACCP tracking built into the same tool as the schedule.
The vendor's support during an inspection.
alternatives: Team schedule for bars and restaurants, free up to 4 employees, hour totals and overrun alerts.
French HACCP software with a free plan (manual temperatures, receiving, traceability); Pro at €49.90 excl. VAT/month with scheduling.
Web and mobile HACCP app with a free starter plan of 4 modules (including temperature readings).
Scheduling and time clocking for independent restaurants with hospitality-agreement checks, flat €39/month whatever the headcount.
komia.prompt:
Build me a staff scheduling and time-clocking tool with a HACCP module, for my venue, to replace a subscription.

Stack: web app (Next.js or Node/Express) with SQLite, hosted on my small server, usable on phone and computer. No mandatory paid service, no telemetry.

Core of the tool:
- Schedule per position with weekly templates, and time clocking from phone or tablet.
- Separate HACCP module: temperature readings and cleaning checklists timestamped by the employee.
- Daily view: who is working, which hygiene tasks remain.

Requirements:
- Weekly schedule by position and by shift, with drag and drop, copy of the previous week and publication to the teams.
- Availability and leave requests entered by the employee, approved by the manager.
- Configurable alerts: 11 h rest between two shifts, 10 h of work per day, weekly working time. Default values from the French Labour Code, to be adapted to the HCR collective agreement by my accountant.
- CSV export of hours per employee and per period, for my accountant.
- Employee data: role-based access (manager, employee), password or magic link, change log.
- HACCP readings: append-only log, never edited or erased; a correction creates a new line (Regulation (EC) 852/2004, food safety plan).

Out of scope: payroll and connection to a temperature probe.

README: installation, backup, and a reminder that this tool is not payroll software and calculates no salary, no DSN, no DPAE, and that legal counts remain to be checked by my accountant.

kooklin.description: Food traceability and HACCP platform for restaurants and central kitchens.
kooklin.justification: Regulation (EC) 852/2004 requires food businesses to have a food safety plan based on HACCP principles, whose records (temperatures, cleaning, receiving) justify that the procedures are applied. The texts consulted set no format (paper or digital) for these records: what matters is that they are reliable and kept. Food traceability (who delivered what, which batch, which use-by date, in which dish) is digitised with structured forms. At €85/month, a custom build pays for itself quickly. The real work is rigour in data entry in the kitchen: a badly designed tool will be bypassed. For a central kitchen with several sites, consolidation takes more.
perdez: Help with setup in the kitchen.
Sheet templates by type of production.
alternatives: French HACCP software with a free plan (manual temperatures, receiving, traceability); Pro at €49.90 excl. VAT/month with scheduling.
Web and mobile HACCP app with a free starter plan of 4 modules (including temperature readings).
HACCP: temperatures, cleaning plan and traceability, from €47 excl. VAT/month billed annually, no commitment.
kooklin.prompt:
Build me a batch-based food traceability log, for my restaurant, to replace a HACCP subscription.

Stack: installable phone web app (PWA, mobile first), Node, Express, SQLite (better-sqlite3), hosted on my small server. No heavy front-end framework.

Core of the tool:
- Receiving: supplier, product, batch number, use-by date, quantity, temperature on receipt, photo of the label.
- Production: a dish or preparation records the batches used, quantity produced, use-by date set.
- Backward search: from a batch, show all the dishes concerned; from a dish, show all the batches.
- Alert when a batch nears its use-by date.
- Non-conformities and supplier recalls, with corrective action.

Common requirements (a reading only counts as evidence if it is reliable):
- Every record is timestamped by the server, with the user. A reading is never edited or erased: a correction creates a new line that points back to the old one (append-only log).
- Deviations (temperature out of range, cleaning not done) trigger a non-conformity to handle: cause, corrective action, closing date.
- Thresholds, zones (cold rooms, hot dishes) and checklists are set in a configuration file, without touching the code.
- PDF export per period, ready to show during a health inspection. Configurable data retention period.
- Several users (PIN code per employee), no email account. No telemetry.
- CSV and PDF export of traceability over a period.

Out of scope: managing several kitchens, purchasing integration, certification.

README: installation, database backup, and a reminder that this tool documents your food safety plan but does not replace it: have it reviewed by your inspection body or a hygiene consultant.

koust.description: Management of purchasing, stock, sales and cost of goods for restaurants and groups.
koust.justification: Stock tracking with thresholds and alerts is easy to rebuild. Koust adds purchasing, sales and cost of goods, with a supplier catalogue and negotiated prices built in: that is the part that remains hard to reproduce alone. It is for you to judge whether your venue needs that catalogue or just a simple product list.
perdez: Automatic import of sales from your till.
The connection to suppliers' catalogues and invoices.
alternatives: Odoo Community edition (LGPL): Inventory, Purchase and Manufacturing (bills of materials) modules for stock and costs.
Free plan: recipe cards, allergens and cost prices; full plan at €159/month per site.
Free, unlimited food-cost calculator for restaurants, with PDF export.
Cost of goods and margin per dish calculated from scanned invoices, from €19 excl. VAT/month.
koust.prompt:
Build me a purchasing, stock and cost-of-goods tool for a restaurant, for my venue, to replace a subscription.

Stack: web app (Next.js or Node/Express) with SQLite, hosted on my small server, usable on phone and computer. No mandatory paid service, no telemetry.

Core of the tool:
- Supplier orders with receiving and checking of quantities received.
- Theoretical stock calculated from sales entered or imported as CSV, and physical inventory to measure the gap.
- Actual cost of goods as a percentage of turnover, per period.

Requirements:
- Units and conversions (kg, g, L, cl, piece); purchase price excl. VAT per product and per supplier, with a history of changes.
- Recipe card per dish: ingredients, weights, losses and yield, cost per portion, selling price incl. VAT, margin in euros and as a percentage.
- VAT configurable per product (for example 10% for catering, 20% for alcohol): to be validated by my accountant, hard-code nothing.
- Allergens: the 14 mandatory allergens ticked per ingredient, and automatically carried onto each recipe card (decree 2015-447).
- CSV import and export (products, suppliers, recipes) so I am not locked in.

Out of scope: direct connection to the till, wholesalers and accounting.

README: installation, database backup, and a reminder that the VAT rates and allergen declarations are to be validated with my accountant and my suppliers.

kouver.description: French table reservation software, with floor plan and an AI voice agent to take calls.
kouver.justification: A reservation form with floor plan can be rebuilt fairly well. Handling no-shows and the AI voice agent that answers the phone are what remain hard to reproduce alone.
perdez: The voice agent that answers the phone.
alternatives: Self-hosted table reservation system (MIT), floor plan, multi-restaurant, no customer account.
Online ordering and table reservations for restaurants, open source (MIT), self-hosted, no commission.
Reservations with no commission, free plan up to 25 reservations a month, French interface (Danish vendor).
Restaurant reservations with no commission, Management pack at €39/month, 14-day trial.
kouver.prompt:
Build me a reservation tool with floor plan, for my venue, to replace a subscription.

Stack: web app (Next.js or Node/Express) with SQLite, hosted on my small server, usable on phone and computer. No mandatory paid service, no telemetry.

Core of the tool:
- Reservation form and floor plan.
- No-show handling: manual blacklist and reminder message.
- Configuration page for hours and services.

Requirements:
- Reservation form embeddable in my site: date, time, number of covers, contact details, remarks.
- Capacity per slot and per service, meal duration by group size, blocked dates, waiting list.
- Confirmation and reminder by email, with a cancellation link; no-show tracking.
- Customer file with GDPR consent, export and deletion on request; spam protection.
- Daily view for service: arrivals, tables, notes.

Out of scope: the AI voice agent that answers the phone and platform integrations.

README: installation, SMTP configuration, GDPR reminder, and a reminder that syncing with Google, TheFork or other platforms is out of scope.

laddition.description: Till and management software for restaurants and bars.
laddition.justification: An NF525-certified till system with stock management, VAT and accounting closings represents regulatory and reliability work that few small businesses have any interest in rebuilding themselves.
alternatives: Open-source ERP (LGPL) whose Point of Sale app handles floor plan, kitchen and QR code. NF525 certification not confirmed for the Community edition: check with the vendor before using it as a till in France.
Self-hosted restaurant till and ordering (AGPL): QR menu, tables, reservations, kitchen screen. No NF525 certification announced: check before using it as a till in France.
NF525-certified online cash register with a free plan, usable in restaurants and retail.
Certified iPad cash register, simpler, aimed at shopkeepers and restaurants.

le-commis.description: Centralisation of Google, Facebook and TripAdvisor reviews with AI-assisted replies, in a restaurant management suite.
le-commis.justification: Collecting reviews by email after the customer's visit is an accessible project; centralising several platforms and adding AI replies takes more maintenance.
perdez: Automatic consolidation of reviews from several platforms.
The other modules of the management suite.
alternatives: Free Google Business Profile: opening hours, posts and replies to customer reviews.
Free Google review collection by QR code for one venue; Pro plan with AI replies at €89 a year.
AI-written replies to Google reviews, Business plan at €19/month for unlimited replies.
le-commis.prompt:
Build me a customer review tracking tool with post-visit email, for my venue, to replace a subscription.

Stack: web app (Next.js or Node/Express) with SQLite, hosted on my small server, usable on phone and computer. No mandatory paid service, no telemetry.

Core of the tool:
- Email sent after the visit with a direct link to my Google listing.
- Manual or CSV-import tracking of Google, Facebook and TripAdvisor reviews, with “replied / to reply” status.
- Reply templates that I adapt myself, with no automatic generation.

Requirements:
- GDPR: explicit consent at collection (unticked box, clear wording), unsubscribe link in every message, export and deletion of a customer on request, configurable retention period.
- Honest reviews: every customer receives the same invitation, with no prior sorting by satisfaction, and no reward is tied to a positive review. The review platforms' rules apply.
- Emails sent through a configurable SMTP server, with rate limiting; no scraping of the review platforms.
- Simple dashboard: invitations sent, clicks, evolution over time.

Out of scope: automatic retrieval of reviews, AI-generated replies and the rest of the management suite.

README: installation, SMTP configuration, GDPR reminder (purposes, legal basis, retention) and a reminder that links to the review platforms are entered by hand.

lemlist.description: Email prospecting tool: personalised sequences sent from your domain, which stop as soon as a prospect replies.
lemlist.justification: Sending a short sequence to a list of prospects you are entitled to contact, stopping on reply and with sending limits, is doable in a few days. What Lemlist sells on top (mailbox warm-up, contact database, enrichment) rests on data and networks that you will not have. In France, email prospecting is regulated by the CNIL and the GDPR: lawful collection, easy opt-out, and no contacts bought from just anyone. The tool is the smallest of the problems.
perdez: Warming up sending mailboxes and deliverability reputation.
The contact database and data enrichment.
alternatives: Open-source marketing automation platform with campaigns, contacts and email flows, including handling of replies, bounces and unsubscribes.
lemlist.prompt:
Build me a small email sequence tool to contact prospects I am entitled to contact, as a modest replacement for Lemlist.

Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL with Drizzle, a transactional email provider that I choose.

To do:
- CSV import only after I have confirmed the lawfulness of the collection and stated the source of the list.
- Contacts with tags, suppression status, consent notes and change history.
- A short sequence with delays, office-hours windows and a per-domain sending limit.
- Provider webhooks (delivery, bounce, complaint, unsubscribe) handled.
- The sequence stops immediately on reply, bounce, complaint, deletion or manual pause.
- Deliverability alerts, total sends per day, mandatory preview before activating a sequence.
- Local launch in one command, secrets in .env, no telemetry, tests, README.

Out of scope: collecting data from protected platforms, buying or generating contacts, automated mailbox warm-up, circumventing providers' limits.

lengow.description: French platform for distributing product catalogues to marketplaces and advertising channels, with sales management, price monitoring and brand protection.
lengow.justification: Exporting a catalogue in the format of one marketplace is doable. Managing more than 90 marketplaces, each with its changing rules, categories to map and error returns, is permanent work. That is precisely what the vendor maintains. For a shop that sells on one marketplace, its native export is often enough.
perdez: Connections to more than 90 marketplaces claimed by the vendor
Mapping of product categories per channel
Updates to the formats required by each channel

lightspeed-restaurant.description: Cloud till and management (KDS, stock, multi-site) for high-volume restaurants and hotels.
lightspeed-restaurant.justification: Kitchen screen, stock and multi-site synchronised in real time, on an NF525-certified base: a package too broad and too regulated for a custom build.
alternatives: Open-source ERP (LGPL) whose Point of Sale app handles floor plan, kitchen and QR code. NF525 certification not confirmed for the Community edition: check with the vendor before using it as a till in France.
Self-hosted restaurant till and ordering (AGPL): QR menu, tables, reservations, kitchen screen. No NF525 certification announced: check before using it as a till in France.
NF525-certified online cash register with a free plan, usable in restaurants and retail.
Certified iPad cash register, simpler, aimed at shopkeepers and restaurants.

linktree.description: A single page to put in your social media bio, grouping all the important links of a person or brand.
linktree.justification: This is the most obvious verdict in the catalogue: a static page, a list of buttons, possibly a click counter. An evening is enough, and hosting costs almost nothing. The only real gap: the editor for non-technical people.
perdez: Integrations (networks, newsletters, shops) that you probably weren't using.
alternatives: Self-hosted alternative to Linktree with an editor, themes and click statistics, in a Docker stack.
Open-source link page with more than 100 buttons in well-known brand colours.
Three free one-page sites; the custom domain is still paid.
linktree.prompt:
Build me a link page for my bio, to replace Linktree.

To do:
- A single static page: avatar, name, short bio and a list of buttons read from a links.json file (title, url, optional emoji). Editing the JSON is how I update the page.
- A clean design, mobile first, with automatic dark mode (prefers-color-scheme) and a discreet hover. One HTML file with its CSS is enough, or Astro only if truly useful.
- Click tracking without a third-party service: each link goes through /go/:slug, which records a row locally (file or SQLite) then redirects with a 302. A /stats page protected by basic authentication (credentials in .env) shows clicks per link.
- Correct Open Graph tags and a generated share image, so the page looks good when shared.
- The deployment steps on a small server with Caddy or nginx.

livestorm.description: Browser-based webinar platform, with attendee registration, replay and engagement statistics.
livestorm.justification: A small webinar with registration and a replay page can run on self-hosted Jitsi for a few dozen people. Livestorm, for its part, sells stability with several hundred or thousand participants, reminder emails that land properly, polls, engagement statistics and marketing integrations. For an open meeting with a few people, replaceable. For a sales webinar that matters, no.
perdez: Reminder emails that actually reach the inbox.
Integrations with CRM and marketing tools.
alternatives: Widely used open-source video conferencing platform, which can be a base for small webinars but is not a complete webinar platform.
livestorm.prompt:
Set up a self-hosted small-webinar system, as a partial replacement for Livestorm, for a few dozen participants.

Stack: Docker Compose, Jitsi Meet (pinned images), dedicated TURN server, Next.js panel with PostgreSQL.

To do:
- A registration page per event, then signed room links per participant that expire.
- A panel to create events, enable the waiting room, limit participants and export the list of registrants.
- A simple replay page, published only if all participants were clearly informed of the recording.
- Connection diagnostics: camera, microphone, browser, bandwidth, TURN reachability.
- Recording disabled by default; consent visible on screen for each participant.
- Audit log, no media without explicit activation.
- Health checks, backup, restore, update.
- Secrets in .env, no telemetry, tests, README.

Out of scope: worldwide delivery network, large-scale webinars, telephony, recording with regulatory value.

localranker.description: Local SEO and reputation management solution for neighbourhood businesses.
localranker.justification: Local SEO depends on external APIs and algorithms (Google first among them) that change regularly: monitoring and ongoing maintenance work, not a one-off development.
alternatives: Free Google Business Profile: opening hours, posts and replies to customer reviews.
Free Google review collection by QR code for one venue; Pro plan with AI replies at €89 a year.
AI-written replies to Google reviews, Business plan at €19/month for unlimited replies.

loom.description: Screen recording with instant hosting: you record, get a link, and the video is transcribed and shareable.
loom.justification: Recording the screen, transcribing locally and publishing the video at a secret URL on your own server is a weekend, and the result is strikingly simple. The rest of Loom (viewing statistics, timestamped comments, per-person access rights, team library) is only useful if you share a lot with a lot of people. For your solo uses, replaceable.
perdez: Reliable hosting, no server to monitor.
Sharing rights per person or per domain.
The team library and the browser extension.
alternatives: Alternative to Loom with your own storage and your own server to manage.
Excellent open-source recording engine; hosting and sharing are still yours to build.
Free screen recorder (GPL-3.0) as a browser extension, no watermark.
loom.prompt:
Build me a screen recording and link sharing tool, to replace Loom on macOS.

Two parts: a local command and a small server on my VPS.

To do:
- `rec start` and `rec stop` around ffmpeg's avfoundation capture (screen + microphone), file saved to ~/Recordings/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM.mp4. No camera bubble.
- On stop: conversion to web-friendly H.264, local transcription with whisper.cpp, then upload of the video and text to the server by rsync over SSH.
- The server (Node, Express, better-sqlite3, behind my reverse proxy) serves each video at an unguessable /v/<random id> URL: player, title, date, transcript below with in-page search.
- `rec stop` prints the URL and copies it to the clipboard. Goal: under a minute between stopping and having the link for a 2-minute video.
