- The stages are a fixed list in the code: prospect, qualified, proposal, negotiation, closed.

Screens:
1. /pipeline: kanban, one column per stage, cards showing title, company and amount. Drag and drop saves the stage; headers show the number of deals and the total amount.
2. /contacts and /companies: tables with search, then a record with linked deals, activity timeline and open tasks.
3. /deals/[id]: edit fields inline, log an activity, mark won or lost.
4. /today: tasks due today or overdue, and deals with no activity for 14 days, flagged “cooling down”.

Also: global search (cmd+K) with SQLite LIKE and no AI; full JSON export (/api/export); contact CSV import with column mapping before confirmation; a seed script (about 20 fictional contacts, 8 companies, 12 deals).

Out of scope: sending or syncing emails, OAuth, multi-user, automations, reports beyond pipeline totals, mobile app, third-party APIs.

README: installation in under five commands and a paragraph on backing up the SQLite file.

salto-ks.description: Cloud access-control platform to remotely manage access to a venue's doors and spaces.
salto-ks.justification: Access control touches the building's physical security and depends on proprietary locks and firmware: it is not software you rebuild, it is a closed system by design.

sellsy.description: French sales management platform (TeamSystem group): CRM, quotes, invoicing, electronic signature and pre-accounting, with electronic invoicing through an approved platform according to the vendor.
sellsy.justification: The CRM, quotes and PDF invoices can be rebuilt without difficulty, and are enough for many freelancers. What you lose: the transmission of invoices through an approved platform, which the electronic invoicing reform will eventually require, and the continuous updating of the rules. If you keep Sellsy for invoicing and build the CRM around it, the compromise is reasonable.
perdez: Pre-accounting and exports for the accountant
alternatives: Free management suite: customers, quotes, invoices, calendar and payment tracking, developed in France.
Free ERP combining CRM, quotes, invoicing and project tracking; heavier to set up.
Modular self-hostable ERP and CRM (free community edition): sales, invoicing, inventory, HR.
sellsy.prompt:
Build me a small sales management tool for a freelancer or very small business, without claiming to replace Sellsy or do official accounting.

Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, SQLite. Data at my place, secrets in .env, no telemetry.

To do:
- Customers and prospects: record, history of exchanges, sales follow-up stage (new, quote sent, won, lost).
- Quote then invoice from the quote, as PDF: continuous numbering with no gaps, mandatory mentions, VAT per line, deposit and balance.
- Invoices are never deleted or edited: a mistake is corrected with a credit note.
- Payment tracking and reminder by email (configurable SMTP).
- Signing of the quote by the customer: unique link, tick box, date and timestamp kept.
- CSV export of customers and invoices for my accountant; simple backup.
- Tests on numbering and totals; README with the limits.

Out of scope: accounting, bank reconciliation, VAT returns, and the transmission of invoices through an approved platform that electronic invoicing reform will eventually require (timetable to be checked). Never state that the documents comply with that reform.

semrush.description: SEO and marketing toolbox: keywords, competition, backlinks, advertising, content and visibility in AI answers.
semrush.justification: Tracking the positions of your own keywords, cross-checking Google Search Console and technically auditing your site is doable in a weekend, for a few euros of API a month. But Semrush sells immense databases collected over years: keywords, competitors, backlinks, estimated traffic. No solo build reproduces them, and scraping is not a clean option. Your tool tracks what belongs to you, not the market.
perdez: The keyword database and their search volumes.
semrush.prompt:
Build me a rank and technical health tracker for the sites I own. It covers the part of Semrush that you can collect yourself.

Stack: a Node CLI run nightly by cron, better-sqlite3 for history, a static HTML report regenerated on each run.

To do:
- Track 20 to 50 keywords through a search results API (Serper or DataForSEO, key in .env): position per keyword and per day, with small evolution charts in the report.
- Fetch clicks, impressions and average position per query from the Google Search Console API, for my own sites (OAuth credentials in .env).
- A technical crawl of my site with crawlee: broken links, missing titles and descriptions, redirect chains, slow pages, in a table in the report.
- A weekly email via Resend (key in .env), sent only if something moved: change of more than 3 places or new 404 errors.
- No accounts, no telemetry, everything in a SQLite file.

Out of scope: keyword gaps with competitors, backlinks and traffic estimates for sites that do not belong to me. No scraping or estimating of third-party data.

README: the cheapest API plan for daily checks, the Search Console OAuth steps, and a reminder that Semrush's advantage is years of data that a solo tool cannot gather.

sendcloud.description: European shipping platform for online shops: label creation, tracking and returns, with more than 170 carriers including Colissimo and Mondial Relay according to the vendor.
sendcloud.justification: Generating a label for one carrier is doable; managing several, with negotiated rates, tracking and returns, is not. Sendcloud's value is in the contracts and the connections to carriers, which change regularly. For a shop that ships a single type of parcel with a single carrier, going directly through that carrier is enough.
perdez: Connections to more than 170 carriers claimed by the vendor

sentry.description: Application error and performance monitoring: groups errors, alerts the team and keeps the context. Free plan for a single developer.
sentry.justification: A small service that receives your application's errors, groups them by type and emails you is simple to build. Sentry adds reading browser error traces from source files, performance monitoring and session replays. For a single project, replaceable; for several applications and teams, keep the tool.
perdez: Reconstructing browser errors from the source code
sentry.prompt:
Build me a small error collector for my web applications, without claiming to replace Sentry.

Stack: Node, TypeScript, SQLite, a JavaScript script to include in my applications.

To do:
- A script that captures unhandled errors (browser and server) and sends them to my collector with the page, browser and time.
- Grouping of identical errors by fingerprint, occurrence counter, first and last seen.
- Interface listing the errors, with status (new, seen, resolved) and trace.
- Email alert for a new error (configurable SMTP), limited to avoid a flood.
- No personal data collected by default (IP addresses not kept); configurable retention period.
- Tests on grouping; README with the limits.

Out of scope: performance monitoring, session replays, source maps.
alternatives: Self-hosted error collector (MIT), compatible with Airbrake clients.
Error tracking, logs and session replays (Apache-2.0), self-hostable.
Simple self-hosted error tracking (MIT), compatible with the Sentry protocol.

sequoiasoft.description: Software suite for managing hotels, outdoor accommodation and wellness centres.
sequoiasoft.justification: Sequoiasoft covers three trades in one piece of software: the hotel, outdoor hospitality and the wellness centre. Outdoor hospitality adds its own rules (pitches, lengths of stay, tourist tax) that differ from a hotel's. Making them coexist with shared invoicing is too wide a scope for custom work; pick the vendor that knows your trade.
alternatives: PMS, booking engine and website for hotels, open source (OSL 3.0 licence), to host yourself.
Management suite for outdoor hospitality: reservations, invoicing, till and access, demo on request.
Campsite management software (reservations, pitch plan, invoicing), licence at €750 excl. VAT.

sevenrooms.description: Reservations, table management and CRM for restaurants and hotel groups.
sevenrooms.justification: Designed for multi-venue groups with CRM and advanced marketing automation, this is an orchestration too broad to be rebuilt by a single business.
alternatives: Open-source table reservation system (MIT), self-hosted with Docker, no per-cover fee.
Reservation management with a free plan (25 reservations/month), then fixed plans from €23/month with no commission.
Table reservations with customer book (Guestbook), plans from €67/month, no commitment.
Online table reservations, available in French, fixed monthly subscription with no per-customer fee.

shine.description: French online business account for freelancers and small businesses, licensed payment institution according to its site, with electronic invoicing and cards.
shine.justification: A business account is a regulated financial service: a licensed institution holds the funds, issues the cards and monitors fraud. No in-house tool can replace that. An expense tracker imported from CSV remains possible; the money itself stays with a licensed institution.
perdez: The account and cards, under a regulator's supervision

shopify.description: Online shop platform: catalogue, payment, orders, shipping and physical till, hosted and maintained by the vendor.
shopify.justification: A mini-shop for a handful of products, with payment delegated to Stripe, can be built in a weekend. But as soon as you sell for real, you inherit European VAT, shipping rates, payment disputes, fraud and the site's availability on sale day. Shopify mostly sells that peace of mind, plus the ecosystem of apps around it. For a real business, this is not a good playground.
perdez: A proven checkout that reassures buyers.
Delivery and VAT modules and the physical till.
Support and holding up under peaks.
alternatives: Open-source commerce platform for custom shops; substantial, but without Shopify's hosted offer.
Shop and back office built on Laravel; hosting and running Laravel are up to you.
Classic PHP commerce solution that covers the essentials without piling on modules.
Modern, full-featured shop; needs a lot of memory (8 GB minimum on Docker) and competent administration.
Very complete shop engine, which assumes substantial infrastructure and operations.
shopify.prompt:
Build me a small self-hosted shop for a few products, the modest version of what Shopify does.

Stack: Node, Express, better-sqlite3, on my VPS.

To do:
- Products are described in products.json (slug, name, price, images, stock). Catalogue and product pages rendered on the server.
- Basket kept in a session cookie. Payment is entirely delegated to Stripe Checkout (keys in .env): card numbers are never touched.
- The Stripe webhook creates the order, removes stock and sends an email to me and to the buyer through Resend (key in .env).
- An /admin page protected by basic authentication: list of orders and a “shipped” button that notifies the buyer, with an optional tracking number.
- Flat-rate shipping fees per zone in a config file. A sold-out product stays visible but can no longer be bought.
- For VAT, use Stripe Tax: write no tax logic.
- No customer accounts, no telemetry.

Out of scope: promo codes, multi-currency, physical till.

README: setting up the Stripe webhook, and a clear warning: I become the anti-fraud service myself, and this is not Shopify. If volume grows, I migrate to Shopify or Medusa rather than growing this project.

silae.description: SaaS payroll and social declaration platform, used by companies and accounting firms.
silae.justification: Payroll and social declarations are shifting regulatory ground (DSN, contributions): a mistake costs far more than the subscription, so this is not a DIY project.
alternatives: Online payslips with no subscription, from €3.90 to €9.90 excl. VAT per payslip, with DSN and accounting exports.

siteminder.description: Tool to synchronise hotel rates and availability across OTAs and booking channels.
siteminder.justification: SiteMinder is a channel manager: it pushes your rates and availability to booking sites and brings back the reservations. Its base plan covers synchronisation; the Plus plan adds a booking engine and website. A one-minute stock gap is enough to sell the same room twice, and every channel connection has to be kept up as the channel changes. Not an in-house project.
alternatives: PMS, channel manager and booking engine for accommodation, from €15.50/month with no commitment.
Channel manager, cloud PMS and booking engine, monthly with no commitment and no commission on direct sales.

skeat.description: Instant mobile ordering and payment, with no app, for restaurants, bars and party venues.
skeat.justification: Ordering and paying without an app requires every payment to be recorded in the restaurant's certified till, with the right VAT lines, including at peak times. The menu and ordering without payment are within your reach; mobile payment linked to the till is not.
alternatives: Open-source platform (MIT, Laravel) for online ordering, table reservation and restaurant management.

Open-source ERP (LGPL) whose Point of Sale app handles floor plan, kitchen and QR code. NF525 certification not confirmed for the Community edition: check with the vendor before using it as a till in France.
French online ordering and QR menu with no commission, free starter plan limited to 20 orders/month.
Click & collect, table ordering by QR code and loyalty, subscription with no commission on turnover.

skello.description: Scheduling and HR rota management for restaurants.
skello.justification: A simple schedule with time clocking can be rebuilt fairly quickly. Compliance with labour law (overtime, mandatory rest, DSN export) is the real work behind it, and needs ongoing legal maintenance.
perdez: Legal alerts kept up to date by the vendor.
The mobile app and the vendor's support.
alternatives: French vendor (formerly Snapshift) of scheduling, time clocking and payroll preparation for hospitality.
Team scheduling and time clocking for restaurants, per-venue flat rate from €29 excl. VAT/month.
skello.prompt:
Build me an HR scheduling tool for a restaurant, for my venue, to replace a subscription.

Stack: web app (Next.js or Node/Express) with SQLite, hosted on my small server, usable on phone and computer. No mandatory paid service, no telemetry.

Core of the tool:
- Schedule with templates and configurable compliance alerts.
- Availability, leave and shift swaps.
- Preview of payroll cost from the hourly rates entered, to steer the schedule.

Requirements:
- Weekly schedule by position and by shift, with drag and drop, copy of the previous week and publication to the teams.
- Availability and leave requests entered by the employee, approved by the manager.
- Configurable alerts: 11 h rest between two shifts, 10 h of work per day, weekly working time. Default values from the French Labour Code, to be adapted to the HCR collective agreement by my accountant.
- CSV export of hours per employee and per period, for my accountant.
- Employee data: role-based access (manager, employee), password or magic link, change log.

Out of scope: payroll and DSN.

README: installation, backup, and a reminder that this tool is not payroll software and calculates no salary, no DSN, no DPAE, and that legal counts remain to be checked by my accountant.

slack-pro.description: Team messaging in channels and threads, with file sharing and search. Pro is the first paid plan.
slack-pro.justification: You can set up a team messaging tool that works, and free alternatives already exist. But what gives Slack its value is its integrations, mobile notifications, calls, and above all the fact that your whole team and partners are already there. A clone does not reproduce that. Count a day for a minimal version, far more for it to be reliable.
perdez: History and search over large volumes.
Controls and security designed for businesses.
alternatives: Slack-like self-hosted messaging for fewer than 250 users; you have to manage PostgreSQL, mail and backups.
Team messaging organised by topic, with full history and good search.
Channels, threads, files and integrations, up to 100 simultaneous users in the Community edition; requires MongoDB.
Matrix protocol client: encrypted rooms, threads, files and calls, usable with a free public account.
Unlimited users, channels and history with 10 GB of storage in total; group meetings and advanced integrations are paid.
slack-pro.prompt:
Build me a private, minimal team messaging for a small group, to replace Slack.

Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL with Drizzle, WebSockets, Docker Compose. No other stack.

To do:
- Public and private channels, threads, reactions, mentions, profiles.
- Messages saved reliably in PostgreSQL; WebSockets are only used to show them live.
- File upload with limited size and sanitised names, and search in the history.
- Owner/member roles, invitations by link, removing a member.
- Reporting, blocking, rate limiting, audit log.
- Data export and backup/restore documented.
- Local launch with a single command, secrets in .env (with a .env.example), no telemetry.
- A few tests on message delivery, plus an end-to-end test of the main flow.

README: installation, architecture, permissions, data location, backup.

sommit.description: Drinks stock management and generation of the wine list, digital or printable.
sommit.justification: A cellar inventory with wine-list generation is a reasonable project: a database of references and page layout, with no particular regulatory constraint.
perdez: Updates to the catalogue of references.
alternatives: Cellar management for restaurateurs (French vendor): stock, up-to-date wine list, digital export, from €29/month.
sommit.prompt:
Build me a drinks stock tool and wine list generator, for my venue, to replace a subscription.

Stack: web app (Next.js or Node/Express) with SQLite, hosted on my small server, usable on phone and computer. No mandatory paid service, no telemetry.

Core of the tool:
- Wine and drink record: producer, appellation, vintage, volume, purchase price, selling price, stock.
- Wine list generated automatically: screen version (web page) and printable PDF version, sorted by region or style.
- Automatic removal of a reference from the list when stock reaches zero.

Requirements:
- Units and conversions (kg, g, L, cl, piece); purchase price excl. VAT per product and per supplier, with a history of changes.
- Recipe card per dish: ingredients, weights, losses and yield, cost per portion, selling price incl. VAT, margin in euros and as a percentage.
- VAT configurable per product (for example 10% for catering, 20% for alcohol): to be validated by my accountant, hard-code nothing.
- Allergens: the 14 mandatory allergens ticked per ingredient, and automatically carried onto each recipe card (decree 2015-447).
- CSV import and export (products, suppliers, recipes) so I am not locked in.
- Prices displayed incl. VAT; volume stated.

Out of scope: the till and accounting.

README: installation, database backup, and a reminder that the VAT rates and allergen declarations are to be validated with my accountant and my suppliers.

spendesk.description: European spend management platform: company payment cards, expense claims, supplier invoices, purchasing and budgets.
spendesk.justification: Payment cards and supplier transfers are regulated financial services, linked to banks. Purchase approval workflows can be rebuilt, but they are useless without the cards and the accounting integrations. For a small team, a spreadsheet and an ordinary bank card are enough; beyond that, it is a vendor's tool.
perdez: Approval of purchases before the spend

square.description: Till and ordering solution for restaurants and bars, linked to payments and online sales.
square.justification: In France, till software must be NF525-certified or covered by a certificate of compliance (article 286 of the French tax code): an in-house till has neither, with a fine of €7,500 per non-compliant system. Square cannot be separated from its payment terminal, which links takings, orders and online sales in one package. It is impossible to reproduce this with an in-house tool: take the whole package or another certified vendor.
alternatives: Open-source ERP (LGPL) whose Point of Sale app handles floor plan, kitchen and QR code. NF525 certification not confirmed for the Community edition: check with the vendor before using it as a till in France.
NF525-compliant online cash register, offered free with optional paid extras, restaurant mode included.
NF525-certified iPad till for restaurants and bars, with click & collect, reservations and pay-at-table.
Certified till software for restaurants, bars and shops, with floor plan, stock and customer accounts.

squarespace.description: Hosted website builder for portfolios, business sites, blogs and online shops.
squarespace.justification: For a portfolio or blog that you update yourself, a static site (Markdown, a few templates, RSS feed, contact form) can be set up in a weekend and costs you only hosting. Squarespace is paid for its templates, visual editor and peace of mind (hosting, certificate, domain). If you are comfortable with a text file and git, replaceable. If you want to edit your site from your phone, no.
perdez: Polished templates and the visual editor.
The built-in online shop and forms.
The proven mobile display and support.
The ability to change your site without touching code.
alternatives: Drag-and-drop page builder with blog and e-commerce, self-hostable.
Free business application suite including website, blog, shop and CRM; administration is heavy.
Visual CMS with blog, pages, forms and e-commerce, installed on PHP hosting.
Shop extension for WordPress, allowing pages, blog, portfolio and online selling without platform fees.
Free content management system, a common alternative to Squarespace for showcase sites and blogs.
squarespace.prompt:
Build me my personal site (portfolio, blog, contact form), to replace Squarespace.

Stack: static site Eleventy, Nunjucks, Markdown.

To do:
- Home, about, project grid and blog. Content lives in content/ as Markdown files with frontmatter (title, date, tags).
- A base layout and partials for the header, footer and cards; system fonts; responsive images with @11ty/eleventy-img; no CSS framework.
- Tag pages and RSS feed generated at build time.
- The contact form POSTs to a small Express server: it emails me (SMTP in .env) and appends each message to data/messages.jsonl. Honeypot field against spam, no captcha.
- `npm run build` produces dist/; `npm run deploy` syncs it by rsync to my VPS, served by Caddy with automatic HTTPS.
- No accounts, no telemetry, no database: the content is in git.

Out of scope: drag-and-drop editor, e-commerce, interchangeable themes.

README: DNS to configure, Caddyfile excerpt, SMTP configuration of the form.

staff-and-go.description: HRIS to manage schedules, working time, absences and payroll variables for teams.
staff-and-go.justification: As soon as a tool touches payroll variables, the risk becomes legal and social: an error on a payslip costs far more than an HRIS subscription.
alternatives: French vendor (formerly Snapshift) of scheduling, time clocking and payroll preparation for hospitality.
Team scheduling and time clocking for restaurants, per-venue flat rate from €29 excl. VAT/month.

stripe.description: Online payment platform: card payments, subscriptions, invoices and transfers. Fees in Europe advertised at 1.5% + €0.25 for standard European cards, with no setup fee or monthly fee.
stripe.justification: Accepting card payments means handling banking data (PCI DSS standard), applying the strong authentication required in Europe and managing fraud and disputes. It is not a module you write: even small sites go through a provider. Use Stripe or an equivalent; build the rest (basket, orders) around it.

stuart.description: On-demand delivery platform letting restaurants organise their local deliveries.
stuart.justification: It is not only software: it is a network of couriers. No code sheet replaces a fleet of delivery riders available on demand.
alternatives: Open-source logistics platform (AGPL) for fleet tracking and dispatch, to organise your own delivery rounds.
Federation of bicycle-delivery cooperatives, some of which in France deliver meals for restaurants.

sumup.description: Till system and mobile payment terminal for cafés and restaurants, with sending to the kitchen.
sumup.justification: Tied to a certified physical payment terminal, this is not only software: hardware, certification and payment reliability rule out a home-made solution outright.
alternatives: Open-source ERP (LGPL) whose Point of Sale app handles floor plan, kitchen and QR code. NF525 certification not confirmed for the Community edition: check with the vendor before using it as a till in France.
NF525-compliant online cash register, offered free with optional paid extras, restaurant mode included.
NF525-certified iPad till for restaurants and bars, with click & collect, reservations and pay-at-table.
Certified touchscreen cash register on iPad, used by restaurants and local shops.

sunday.description: Pay at the table by QR code for restaurants.
sunday.justification: Paying at the table is not just a page linked to Stripe: the payment must be recorded in the restaurant's till, itself certified or attested compliant (NF525), and the receipt comes from that till. Redoing this integration for each till, handling split bills, tips and disputes in the middle of service goes beyond a custom project.
alternatives: Open-source ERP (LGPL) whose Point of Sale app handles floor plan, kitchen and QR code. NF525 certification not confirmed for the Community edition: check with the vendor before using it as a till in France.
Ordering and payment by QR code with no till to connect and no commission, subscription from €19.90/month excluding Stripe fees.
Digital menu and order-and-pay by QR code at the table, subscription from €29/month plus transaction fees.

supabase.description: Hosted Postgres database with authentication, file storage and API, open source and self-hostable. Free plan with projects paused after a week of inactivity.
supabase.justification: For a small project, a SQLite or Postgres database with simple authentication is enough and keeps you in control of your data. What Supabase brings: turnkey authentication (sign-in by email, social networks), row-level access rules, file storage and managed backups. A home-made tool works as long as you handle passwords and backups well.
alternatives: Free backend (MIT) in a single executable: SQLite database, authentication, file storage and API.
The same product as open source (Apache-2.0), installable with Docker on your own server.
Self-hostable backend (BSD-3): database, authentication, storage and functions.
supabase.prompt:
Build me a small self-hosted backend for a web application, without claiming to replace Supabase.

Stack: Node, TypeScript, SQLite (or Postgres if I specify), hosted on my small server.

To do:
- Authentication by email and password: hashed passwords (argon2), sessions by secure cookie, reset by email.
- REST API on my tables with per-user access rules (each person reads and writes only their own rows).
- File storage on disk with size and type limits.
- Daily database backup and a tested restore procedure.
- Login log, limit on the number of attempts.
- Tests on the access rules; README with the update procedure.

Out of scope: social-network authentication, real time, serverless functions.

swile.description: French employee benefits card: digital meal vouchers, gift vouchers and business travel, with an app to track your budget.
swile.justification: Meal vouchers fall under a legal framework: issuing, safeguarding employees' funds, the network of merchants that accept them. No company has any interest in building that in-house. What you can build is a sheet to track your benefits; issuing the card remains with a licensed issuer.
perdez: Issuing and safeguarding the funds behind the vouchers
The network of merchants that accept the card
The mobile app and budget tracking
Administrative management on the employer side

systeme-io.description: Suite for online entrepreneurs: sales funnels, emailing, course hosting, payment and affiliate programme in a single subscription.
systeme-io.justification: No single building block is hard on its own: a sales page, a sign-up, a Stripe payment, a protected course area, a referral cookie. A weekend is enough for a first working funnel. The invisible work is elsewhere: deliverability, handling bounces, compliant unsubscribing, VAT on international sales. And you lose the visual editor, which seems secondary until the day you need to change a headline at 11 p.m. without touching code. Worthwhile if you like building, dangerous if it is your only sales channel.
perdez: Visual page and email editors, and the template library.
Managed deliverability: shared reputation, bounces, spam complaints.
Full affiliate programme, with commission payouts and a space for your affiliates.
Webinars, blog and extras included in the subscription.
A single contact when payment fails on launch day.
systeme-io.prompt:
Build me a sales funnel and course platform for a single operator, to replace Systeme.io.

Stack: Next.js (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite (better-sqlite3, SQL migrations in ./migrations), Stripe Checkout and webhooks, Resend for emails. No authentication provider: magic link by email for buyers, an administrator password in .env.

To do:
1. Funnel pages in MDX in ./content/pages (slug, title, hook, button, optional priceId), rendered on the server.
2. Sign-up form to /api/optin. Contacts in SQLite (email, name, tags, source page, creation date, unsubscribe date). Optional double opt-in.
3. Email engine: broadcasts and sequences (JSON files in ./content/sequences: delay, subject, MDX body). A worker (node-cron, every minute) sends due steps and logs everything. Every email has a one-click unsubscribe link and List-Unsubscribe headers.
4. Payment: /api/checkout creates the Stripe session. The webhook grants access to the course on purchase and removes it on refund.
5. A /learn area: modules and lessons in MDX, protected by the purchased access, video by embed URL, progress tracking.
6. Affiliation: /r/CODE sets a 60-day cookie, the sale is attributed through the webhook, commissions are listed with a “pending” status. No payouts.
7. /admin administration: contacts with search, broadcast editor with test send, sales, commissions, CSV exports.

Out of scope: drag-and-drop editors, webinars, blog, VAT management, affiliate payouts, external analytics.

Secrets in .env. Demo data (two contacts, one course, one sequence). README with the Stripe CLI command to test webhooks and deployment on a VPS.
alternatives: Open-source marketing automation (emails, forms, segments, journeys), self-hostable.
Publishing, newsletters and paid subscriptions, with no commission on your revenue (MIT).
Custom online store engine (MIT), to build your own online shop.

tabesto.description: Ordering kiosks, table tablets and integrated touchscreen till for fast food and table service.
tabesto.justification: The package of hardware kiosks + payment + sync with the till and kitchen is an integration project far heavier than a simple digital menu.
alternatives: Open-source ERP (LGPL) whose Point of Sale app handles floor plan, kitchen and QR code. NF525 certification not confirmed for the Community edition: check with the vendor before using it as a till in France.
French specialist in ordering kiosks, with touchscreen tills, kitchen screens and management software for restaurants.

tactill.description: iPad or iPhone till used notably by food shops and restaurants.
tactill.justification: In France, till software must be NF525-certified or covered by a certificate of compliance (article 286 of the French tax code): an in-house till has neither, with a fine of €7,500 per non-compliant system. Tactill, on iPad or iPhone, is used notably by food shops and restaurants. Its ease of use hides a takings log that must be tamper-proof. Go with the vendor.
alternatives: Open-source ERP (LGPL) whose Point of Sale app handles floor plan, kitchen and QR code. NF525 certification not confirmed for the Community edition: check with the vendor before using it as a till in France.
NF525-compliant online cash register, offered free with optional paid extras, restaurant mode included.
NF525-certified iPad till for restaurants and bars, with click & collect, reservations and pay-at-table.
Certified till software for restaurants, bars and shops, with floor plan, stock and customer accounts.

tally.description: Form builder with a document-like editor, a generous free plan and a few paid options such as removing the branding.
tally.justification: A form that records responses, sends them by email or webhook and exports them as CSV is a classic application: a weekend is enough. Tally is generous on the free plan, so the saving is mainly for those who pay to remove the branding or connect a domain. It is for you to judge whether it is worth a weekend of development and a server to watch.
perdez: The polished editor, usable by everyone.

- Thresholds, zones (cold rooms, hot dishes) and checklists are set in a configuration file, without touching the code.
- PDF export per period, ready to show during a health inspection. Configurable data retention period.
- Several users (PIN code per employee), no email account. No telemetry.
- Offline mode with deferred sync, for cellars and cold rooms with no network.

Out of scope: connected probes, several venues, certification.

webflow.justification: For your own sites, a static generator based on YAML blocks, with content in git, is simpler, faster and costs almost nothing to host. What you lose is the visual editor, precisely what designers and clients pay Webflow for: changing a page without touching code. If the site is your own, replaceable. If it is delivered to a client who must edit it alone, no.
perdez: The visual editor close to what a designer does.
Handing the site over to a client who edits it themselves.
alternatives: Open-source visual builder with visual CSS, reusable components and CMS data; free custom domain only when self-hosted.
Hosted visual builder and CMS, free custom domains; the Plasmic branding stays displayed on the free plan and the model relies on React.
In-context page editing, blocks, collections and workflows; more conventional design freedom.
Drag-and-drop pages and CMS content in a PHP application, with a hosted option.
Complete visual CMS with custom content, forms and publishing; less design polish.
webflow.prompt:
Build me a block-based showcase site generator, to replace Webflow on my own sites.

Stack: Eleventy (static site), Nunjucks, YAML.

To do:
- A page is a YAML file that lists blocks: hero, feature grid, testimonial, pricing table, FAQ, call to action, footer. Each block is a Nunjucks partial. I build a page by editing YAML, not HTML.
- CMS-style collections without a CMS: blog posts and case studies in Markdown with frontmatter, list and detail pages generated at build time.
- A single file of design variables (colours, type scale, spacing): a style change touches only one file.
- Responsive by default (every block works at 360 px and at 1280 px), images optimised with @11ty/eleventy-img.
- Forms POST to a small Express server that emails me (SMTP in .env).
- Build into dist/, deployment by rsync to my VPS behind Caddy. Sitemap and OpenGraph tags per page.
- Content in git, no accounts, no telemetry.

Out of scope: drag-and-drop visual editor, handover to a client. If I need visual editing, I self-host Webstudio.

README: reference of the blocks with a complete example page, DNS and Caddy.

weglot.description: Website translation solution: generates multilingual versions of the site, hosted and indexed.
weglot.justification: For a small static site, managing your own translation files with per-language URLs (/fr/, /en/) is a very good choice: you keep control of the text and of SEO, and have no subscription. Weglot is paid for automatic content detection, built-in machine translation, hosting of the translated pages and managed SEO. Replaceable if you have a simple site and a few languages. If the site changes every day, no.
perdez: Automatic detection and translation of the site's content.
The option to order professional translations.
weglot.prompt:
Build me a translation system for a small static site, to replace Weglot.

Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL with Drizzle, an optional machine translation API.

To do:
- Projects, languages, keys, namespaces, descriptions, screenshots, translations and review statuses.
- JSON, YAML, PO and XLIFF import and export, preserving variables and plural forms.
- Generation of localised routes (/fr/, /en/…) at deployment, with hreflang tags and a sitemap per language.
- Glossary, filter for missing strings, translation memory, comments, reviewers.
- Machine translation only applies to the strings I select, with provider, cost and source text visible before approval.
- Pull and push endpoints by token for CI, immutable change log, backups.
- Local launch in one command, secrets in .env, no telemetry, tests, README.

Out of scope: translator marketplace, website translation proxy, enterprise integrations.

wix.description: Website builder with templates, AI tools, online shop, bookings and apps.
wix.justification: If you only need your own site (home, services, about, contact), a static site fits in a weekend, loads faster and costs almost nothing to host. What you lose: the visual editor for changing things without touching code, and the shop, booking and app modules. If you like editing a text file and pushing with git, replaceable. If someone else has to update the site, no.
perdez: The built-in online shop and reservations.
Templates, hosting and managed domain names.
alternatives: Open-source site platform (GPL-2.0 or later) with themes, extensions and an editor; bookings and commerce come through your choice of extensions.
Open-source (MIT licence) drag-and-drop site and shop builder, with a smaller ecosystem of apps.
Open-source business application suite (LGPL-3.0) with website, online commerce and CRM, more complex to administer.
Open-source visual CMS (AGPL-3.0) with blog, shop and extensions, to install on PHP hosting.
wix.prompt:
Build me the website for my business, to replace Wix: the only site I need, not a site builder.

Stack: static site Astro.

To do:
- Pages: home, services, about, contact. The texts live in Markdown and YAML files: changing a text never touches the layout code.
- A single stylesheet, mobile first, with CSS variables for the brand colours and typography. No CSS framework.
- The contact form POSTs to a small Express server: it emails me through SMTP (credentials in .env) and appends a row to data/messages.jsonl. Honeypot field against spam.
- SEO basics at build time: sitemap.xml, robots.txt, title, meta and Open Graph tags per page, and a LocalBusiness JSON-LD block with hours and address.
- `npm run build` then rsync of dist/ to my VPS, served by Caddy with automatic HTTPS.
- No accounts, no telemetry, no administration: changes go through git.
- For appointment booking, link to my booking tool; do not build a booking engine.

Out of scope: drag-and-drop editing, app store, e-commerce. If the business needs a real shop, that is a subject for Shopify.

README: DNS records, Caddy configuration excerpt, list of files to edit for common text changes.

wordpress.description: The open-source CMS behind a large part of the web, with a paid hosted version and a huge choice of extensions.
wordpress.justification: For a blog or showcase site run by one person, a home-made CMS (Markdown, images, drafts, RSS feed, sitemap) can be set up in a weekend. But WordPress is already free and self-hostable: the real question is not “how much do I pay”, it is “do I want to maintain my own CMS rather than a system every freelancer knows”. As soon as there is a shop, a form or a client to hand over to, simply install WordPress.
perdez: Extensions (SEO, forms, cache, statistics, backups) that install in one click.
WooCommerce and everything that looks like commerce.
The block editor and page builders for non-technical people.
The option of handing the site to any developer.
wordpress.prompt:
Build me a self-hosted personal CMS for a single author, to replace WordPress. Empty folder, no cloud service, no telemetry.

Stack: Node 22, TypeScript, Fastify, SQLite (better-sqlite3, file ./data/cms.db), Eta server-side templates, markdown-it (with code highlighting and HTML sanitising). No client framework.

To do:
- Posts and pages: title, slug, Markdown body, excerpt, tags, status (draft, scheduled, published), publication date.
- Administration at /admin: one cookie session, a single administrator, password hash in .env. Editor with live preview, saving as draft, publishing, deletion with confirmation.
- Image upload (resized with sharp) with a button that pastes the Markdown into the post.
- Public routes: paginated home, /posts/:slug, /:slug, /tags/:tag. Feed /feed.xml, /sitemap.xml, OpenGraph tags.
- Full-text search (FTS5). Scheduled posts appear on time, without cron.
- Import of a folder of Markdown files with YAML frontmatter, to load a converted WordPress export.
- `npm run backup`: dated archive of the database and files.

Out of scope: extensions, themes, comments, multi-user, e-commerce, block editor.

README: installation, generating the password hash, running behind Caddy with TLS. A sample-data script (three posts, one page).
alternatives: Publishing, newsletters and paid subscriptions, with no commission on your revenue (MIT).
Very fast static site generator (Apache-2.0), content in text files.
Framework for fast websites (MIT), for those who prefer code to a visual editor.

yavin.description: Takings and payment tracking solution by terminal, with features designed for restaurateurs.
yavin.justification: A certified payment terminal follows the same logic as NF525 tills: the hardware and certification weigh more than the software.
alternatives: Open-source ERP (LGPL) whose Point of Sale app handles floor plan, kitchen and QR code. NF525 certification not confirmed for the Community edition: check with the vendor before using it as a till in France.
NF525-compliant online cash register, offered free with optional paid extras, restaurant mode included.
NF525-certified iPad till for restaurants and bars, with click & collect, reservations and pay-at-table.
Certified till software for restaurants, bars and shops, with floor plan, stock and customer accounts.

yokitup.description: Stock, supplier order, inventory and cost-of-goods management for restaurants.
yokitup.justification: Yokitup covers stock, supplier orders, inventories and cost of goods. Phone-based inventory and cost calculation are affordable in-house. Large-scale supplier management is less so. An independent venue can do without it; a group gains a lot from it.
alternatives: French vendor (Brest) of stock management, recipe cards and margins for restaurants, from €80/month per site.
French ERP for restaurateurs in modules (stock, recipe cards, supplier orders), from €49 excl. VAT/month per module.
yokitup.prompt:
Build me a stock, supplier order, inventory and cost-of-goods tool, for my venue, to replace a subscription.

Stack: web app (Next.js or Node/Express) with SQLite, hosted on my small server, usable on phone and computer. No mandatory paid service, no telemetry.

Core of the tool:
- Rolling inventories on phone, per area, with quick entry.
- Supplier orders with history and delivery tracking.
- Cost of goods per period, compared with turnover entered, with inventory gaps.

Requirements:
- Units and conversions (kg, g, L, cl, piece); purchase price excl. VAT per product and per supplier, with a history of changes.
- Recipe card per dish: ingredients, weights, losses and yield, cost per portion, selling price incl. VAT, margin in euros and as a percentage.
- VAT configurable per product (for example 10% for catering, 20% for alcohol): to be validated by my accountant, hard-code nothing.
- Allergens: the 14 mandatory allergens ticked per ingredient, and automatically carried onto each recipe card (decree 2015-447).
- CSV import and export (products, suppliers, recipes) so I am not locked in.

Out of scope: the till, accounting and wholesalers.

README: installation, database backup, and a reminder that the VAT rates and allergen declarations are to be validated with my accountant and my suppliers.

zapier.description: No-code automation platform: an event in one app triggers an action in another, among thousands of tools.
zapier.justification: Five or six automations that really matter to you are doable: a script, a cron, a webhook. Zapier, for its part, sells more than 9,000 already-authenticated connectors, automatic retries, a clear history and an interface anyone can use. If you are comfortable with code, you save money. Otherwise, you mostly lose maintenance time.
perdez: Maintaining OAuth connections when an API changes.
An interface usable by someone who doesn't code.
Service availability, with nothing to monitor.
alternatives: MIT-licensed community edition, self-hostable with Docker, with no task counter.
Very complete self-hostable automation tool under a “fair-code” licence, not open source in the strict sense.
Self-hosted automation agents (MIT): watch the web and trigger actions.
zapier.prompt:
Build me a small personal automation runner to replace Zapier, limited to the few flows I really use.

Stack: a single Node process on my VPS. Express for incoming webhooks, node-cron for scheduled tasks.

To do:
- A flow = a JS file in pipelines/ that exports its trigger (cron expression or webhook path) and an async run(payload) function.
- The steps are code: fetch() calls to the APIs I want, keys in .env. Adding an integration means writing about twenty lines.
- Each run is logged in SQLite: flow, payload, status, duration, error. On failure, 3 retries with increasing wait (p-retry).
- A /runs page, reachable locally, with the last 100 runs, the detail of the payload or error, and a button to rerun.
- After the last failure, send me a notification on an ntfy topic defined in .env.
- Each webhook URL contains a secret token specific to the flow; everything else is rejected.
- Two examples: a daily 8 am cron flow (weather, then ntfy) and a webhook flow (POST received, row added to a CSV).

Out of scope: visual interface, connector catalogue, third-party OAuth (token APIs only). Each service that requires OAuth costs an afternoon, to be written in the README.

README: systemd unit, adding a flow, .env variables.

zatyoo.description: Certified till for restaurants and bars, with floor plan, stock and customer accounts.
zatyoo.justification: NF525 certification is explicitly highlighted: that is the classic signal that it is better to pay a vendor than rebuild it yourself.
alternatives: Open-source ERP (LGPL) whose Point of Sale app handles floor plan, kitchen and QR code. NF525 certification not confirmed for the Community edition: check with the vendor before using it as a till in France.
NF525-compliant online cash register, offered free with optional paid extras, restaurant mode included.
NF525-certified iPad till for restaurants and bars, with click & collect, reservations and pay-at-table.
Certified touchscreen cash register on iPad, used by restaurants and local shops.

zelty.description: Complete cloud till for independent restaurants and multi-venue chains.
zelty.justification: In France, till software must be NF525-certified or covered by a certificate of compliance (article 286 of the French tax code): an in-house till has neither, with a fine of €7,500 per non-compliant system. Zelty is a complete cloud till for independent restaurants and chains, with several venues to synchronise. Multi-site adds to the difficulty. Go with the vendor.
alternatives: Open-source ERP (LGPL) whose Point of Sale app handles floor plan, kitchen and QR code. NF525 certification not confirmed for the Community edition: check with the vendor before using it as a till in France.
NF525-compliant online cash register, offered free with optional paid extras, restaurant mode included.
NF525-certified iPad till for restaurants and bars, with click & collect, reservations and pay-at-table.
Certified till software for restaurants, bars and shops, with floor plan, stock and customer accounts.
Certified touchscreen cash register on iPad, used by restaurants and local shops.

zenchef.description: Online reservation platform and floor management for restaurants.
zenchef.justification: Online reservation taking is easily rebuilt with a form and a shared calendar. Real-time floor management and multi-platform sync (Google, TheFork) take more work to maintain yourself. Note that Zenchef now brings together Formitable (merger announced in 2024) and Resengo (whose site redirects to Zenchef).
alternatives: Open-source (MIT) table reservation management, self-hostable, multi-restaurant.
Table reservations with no commission, free plan limited to 25 reservations a month, interface available in French.
Restaurant reservation software with no per-cover commission, from €39/month, 14-day trial.
French reservation software hosted in France, €60 excl. VAT/month, no per-cover commission.
French reservation software with no commission, from €89 excl. VAT/month, with deposits and Reserve with Google integration.
zenchef.prompt:
Build me an online reservation tool with floor management, for my venue, to replace a subscription.

Stack: web app (Next.js or Node/Express) with SQLite, hosted on my small server, usable on phone and computer. No mandatory paid service, no telemetry.

Core of the tool:
- Online reservation form and shared calendar.
- Real-time floor plan, with table status (free, occupied, to clean).
- Customer record with history.

Requirements:
- Reservation form embeddable in my site: date, time, number of covers, contact details, remarks.
- Capacity per slot and per service, meal duration by group size, blocked dates, waiting list.
- Confirmation and reminder by email, with a cancellation link; no-show tracking.
- Customer file with GDPR consent, export and deletion on request; spam protection.
- Daily view for service: arrivals, tables, notes.

Out of scope: syncing with Google and TheFork and management of third-party platforms.

README: installation, SMTP configuration, GDPR reminder, and a reminder that syncing with Google, TheFork or other platforms is out of scope.

zendesk.description: Customer support software: shared inbox for emails and web messages, tickets and conversation history.
zendesk.justification: A shared inbox with tickets, assignment and a chat widget is doable in a few days, and Chatwoot or Zammad already do it, for free. But at €55/month/user, Zendesk sells omnichannel (social networks, messaging apps, phone), smart routing, reports and compliance, which only make sense for a structured support team. For 2 or 3 people who reply by email, replaceable. For a real support centre, no.
perdez: Routing between channels: email, chat, social networks, phone.
alternatives: Support inbox with chat, email and help centre, hosted or self-hosted (PostgreSQL and Redis).
Complete ticketing system with email, chat, SLAs and knowledge base; rather heavy self-hosting stack.
Team mailbox with assignment, notes and collision alerts; several add-on modules are paid.
Compact email and live chat support tool with PostgreSQL; a young project.
Free live chat, tickets and help centre; removing the tawk.to branding is paid.
zendesk.prompt:
Build me a customer support tool for a small team, to replace Zendesk.

Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL with Drizzle, WebSockets, Docker Compose.

To do:
- Receive emails and web messages, route them to a shared ticket inbox, reply from a single place, with a searchable history and an audit log.
- A chat widget for websites: reconnection, unread counter, file limits, availability status.
- Filters, alert when two agents open the same ticket, internal notes, canned replies.
- Email and browser notifications, immutable log of assignments and statuses.
- Anti-spam, configurable retention period, export and deletion of a contact (GDPR).
- Docker Compose, backups, health checks, migrations, administrator recovery procedure.
- Secrets in .env, no telemetry, tests, README.

Out of scope: multiple social channels, AI agents trained on support data, agent scheduling, SSO and enterprise compliance.

zoho-crm.description: CRM from the Zoho suite: contacts, companies, deals and sales pipeline, linked to the suite's other tools.
zoho-crm.justification: A sales pipeline with contacts, notes, tasks and next actions can be built in a few days, and free CRMs (Twenty, EspoCRM) already do it. Zoho CRM is worth it mainly for the suite around it: email, accounting, support, automations, reports. If you only use the CRM, replaceable. If you are in the Zoho suite, leaving the CRM breaks the rest.
perdez: The rest of the Zoho suite (email, accounting, support).
Automatic capture of emails and calendars.
alternatives: Modern CRM with custom objects, views and mailbox sync, self-hostable with Docker Compose.
Traditional CRM with an editable data model; to host and administer yourself.
Complete old-school CRM with all the classic modules, on a LAMP or LEMP stack.
Free hosted CRM for two users, limited to 1,000 contacts, with little customisation and automation.
Board of leads and deals with notes, tasks and emails, narrower than Zoho CRM on automation and reports.
zoho-crm.prompt:
Build me a personal CRM to replace Zoho CRM, without recreating the rest of the suite.

Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL with Drizzle, Docker Compose.

To do:
- Contacts, companies, deals, notes, tasks and configurable pipeline stages.
- Fast global search, duplicate detection and merging, CSV import and export.
- Interaction timeline with manual entry of emails and meetings.
- Saved views, filters, owner per deal, dashboard of next actions.
- Access roles, immutable activity log, backups, recovery command.
- A realistic demo space and documentation of field mapping for imports.
- Local launch in one command, secrets in .env, no telemetry, tests, README.

Out of scope: automatic mailbox reading, commercial enrichment databases, forecasts, enterprise compliance.

zoom-pro.description: Video meetings and workspace; the Pro plan is Zoom's first paid plan.
zoom-pro.justification: For meetings with a few people, a self-hosted Jitsi instance does the job, and you keep your data at home. But Zoom is above all a worldwide network that keeps good picture quality even when connections are poor, plus recording, transcription, call numbers and integrations. That is what drives the price, and what cannot be reproduced alone. A good deal for internal calls, a bad one for clients or webinars.
perdez: A worldwide network that stays smooth even on poor connections.
Integrations with calendars and business tools, and support.
alternatives: Open-source video conferencing: you share a room link and meet, without Zoom's business features.
WebRTC room deployable as a Docker stack, with waiting room, whiteboard and recording; AGPL licence.
Calls and chat built into Nextcloud; heavier calls need a TURN server and some network work.
zoom-pro.prompt:
Set up private, self-hosted video conferencing rooms, to replace Zoom Pro, for small meetings.

Stack: Docker Compose, Jitsi Meet (pinned images), dedicated TURN server, Next.js control panel with PostgreSQL.

To do:
- Deploy Jitsi Meet and TURN, local launch in one documented command.
- A panel to create rooms, issue signed invitation links that expire, enable the waiting room and limit participants.
- A diagnostics page: camera, microphone, browser, bandwidth, TURN reachability.
- Recording disabled by default; if enabled, visible on-screen consent for each participant.
- Room metadata and audit log kept, no media without explicit activation.
- Health checks, bandwidth dashboard, backup, restore, update, incident handling.
- Secrets in .env, no telemetry, tests, README.

Out of scope: worldwide media network, large-scale webinars, telephony, recording with regulatory value, guaranteed support.

github.description: Code hosting and collaboration around Git: repositories, pull requests, issues, continuous integration (Actions) and the Copilot assistant. Free plan with unlimited private repositories and 2,000 CI minutes a month.
github.justification: Hosting your Git repositories on your own server is half a day with Forgejo or Gitea: pull requests, issues and CI are already there. What you lose: the network effect (everyone has an account, contributors and clients are there), the ecosystem of ready-made actions and the availability of a managed service. For solo use or a small closed team, replaceable; for open source open to contributions, no.
perdez: The network effect: contributors, clients and recruiters are already there
The ecosystem of ready-made CI actions
The availability and backups of a managed service
Copilot and the built-in security tools
github.prompt:
Set up a self-hosted Git server to replace GitHub for my private repositories.

Do not develop a forge: deploy Forgejo (or Gitea) on my VPS.

alternatives: Lightweight Git forge (MIT), self-hostable: repositories, pull requests, issues, built-in CI.
Very lightweight self-hosted Git service (MIT): repositories, issues, pull requests.
Self-hosted Git forge with built-in CI/CD (MIT): repositories, issues, pull requests.

postman.description: Platform to design, test and document APIs: request client, collections, mock servers and monitoring. Free plan; Solo plan at $9 a month, Team at $19 per user.
postman.justification: An HTTP request client with collections, environment variables and history is very easy to replace: Bruno and Hoppscotch are free software and already do the essentials, with no mandatory account. What you lose: team sync, scheduled monitoring and hosted mock servers. For solo use, this is one of the easiest replacements in the catalogue.
postman.prompt:
Build me a small local HTTP request client to replace Postman in my solo use.

Stack: local web app (Node, Express, plain JavaScript), collections stored as JSON files in a folder versioned by git.

To do:

- Environment variables (dev, prod) with {{variable}} substitution, secrets read from .env and never written to the files.
- Response display: status, duration, size, headers, formatted body, copy as curl.
- Simple assertions on the response (status, JSON field equal to) runnable across a whole collection, with a summary.
- Import of a Postman collection (v2.1 format) and of an OpenAPI file.
- History of the last 100 requests; localhost only, no account or telemetry.

Out of scope: team sync, scheduled monitoring, hosted mock servers.

README: launch, collection format, and a reminder that Bruno or Hoppscotch already do this if I prefer to maintain nothing.
alternatives: Free API client (MIT) whose collections are plain files in your git repository, usable without an account.
Free API client (MIT) in the browser, self-hostable, with collections and environment variables.
API client for testing requests (Apache-2.0), an alternative to Postman.

netlify.description: Hosting and deployment platform for websites and web applications, with deployments on every commit, functions and forms. Free plan with limited credits; Pro plan at $20 a month.
netlify.justification: For a static site, a web server, a deployment script and a proxy do the job. Netlify brings deployment on every commit, branch previews, the worldwide delivery network, forms and serverless functions with nothing to manage. Replaceable for a showcase site you rarely change; less so for a team that deploys ten times a day.
perdez: Deployment on every commit and branch previews
Forms and serverless functions with nothing to manage
netlify.prompt:
Build me a self-hosted static site deployment to replace Netlify.

Stack: a small Linux server, Caddy, a small Node service to receive webhooks, GitHub Actions or Forgejo.

- Each site lives in /srv/sites/<name>/; Caddy serves the current folder through a symbolic link, automatic HTTPS, one subdomain per site.

- One preview per branch at <branch>.<name>.mydomain, removed when the branch is closed.
- A forms endpoint: POST received, honeypot anti-spam, email sent through configurable SMTP.
- Simple monitoring (site online, disk space) with email alert.

Out of scope: worldwide delivery network, serverless functions, A/B tests.

README: adding a site, rollback, DNS and server configuration.
alternatives: Free platform (Apache-2.0) to install on your server to deploy sites, applications and databases.
Deployment platform on your server (Apache-2.0): apps, databases and HTTPS in a few clicks.
Mini-PaaS on a single server (MIT): git push to deploy.

firebase.description: Google's platform for applications: authentication, Firestore database, hosting, file storage, functions and messaging. Free Spark plan; Blaze plan pay-as-you-go.
firebase.justification: For a small application, a SQLite or Postgres database with simple authentication and file storage is enough, and PocketBase already does all that in a single executable. What Firebase brings: turnkey authentication, real-time sync with offline mode on mobile, push notifications and automatic scaling. Replaceable for a classic website or web app; less so for a real-time mobile app.
perdez: Real-time sync with offline mode on mobile
firebase.prompt:
Build me a small self-hosted backend for a web application, to replace Firebase.

Stack: Node, TypeScript, SQLite, hosted on my small server.

To do:
- Authentication by email and password (argon2), sessions by secure cookie, reset by email.
- REST API on my collections with per-user access rules, validated by a schema.
- Subscription to real-time changes through Server-Sent Events.
- File storage on disk with size and type limits.
- Daily database backup and a tested restore procedure.
- Tests on the access rules; README with the update procedure.

Out of scope: push notifications, offline on mobile, serverless functions, social-network authentication.
alternatives: Free backend (MIT) in a single executable: SQLite database, authentication, file storage, API and real time.
PostgreSQL database, authentication and storage (Apache-2.0), self-hostable.
Self-hostable backend (BSD-3): database, authentication, storage and functions.

clerk.description: Authentication and user management service for applications: sign-in, two-factor authentication, enterprise SSO. Free plan up to 50,000 retained active users; Pro at $25 a month.
clerk.justification: An email and password sign-in can be coded in an evening; the real difficulty is everything around it: safe reset, two-factor authentication, bot detection, revocable sessions, enterprise SSO. In security, doing it badly is worse than not doing it. If you want to keep control, a free library like Better Auth does the job; writing authentication yourself is not recommended.
perdez: Turnkey two-factor authentication and bot detection
alternatives: Free authentication library (MIT) for TypeScript: email, social sign-in, two-factor authentication, sessions.

resend.description: Email sending service by API or SMTP, for transactional and marketing messages. Free plan with 3,000 emails a month (100 a day); Pro at $20 a month.
resend.justification: Sending an email is easy; getting it into the inbox is not: sender reputation, a properly configured domain (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), handling bounces and complaints. A home-made sending server ends up in spam. The right compromise is to use a provider (Resend, Amazon SES, Brevo) and build around it: templates, queues, tracking.

cursor.description: Code editor with built-in AI agents, code review and collaboration. Free Hobby plan; Pro at $20 a month, Teams at $40 per user.
cursor.justification: A code editor is a huge project, and what makes Cursor valuable is access to leading AI models, integration in the editor and agents that edit several files. None of that can be reproduced alone. What you can do: plug your own API key into a free editor; you keep the editor, you change the model provider.
perdez: Access to leading AI models included in the subscription

algolia.description: Search service for sites and applications: keyword and semantic search, ranking, personalisation and recommendations. Free plan with 10,000 search requests a month and 50,000 records.

proton-vpn.description: Swiss VPN service with open-source, audited apps, more than 2,000 servers in more than 140 countries; free plan limited to one device.
proton-vpn.justification: A personal VPN is easy to set up: WireGuard on a VPS protects you on public Wi-Fi. But a service like Proton VPN sells something else: thousands of servers in dozens of countries, a no-logs policy audited by third parties and the ability to choose the exit. A VPN on your own server does not make you anonymous: your provider sees everything that goes through it.

The ability to choose the exit country

What you lose: filtering of bots and junk traffic, goals and funnels, Search Console integration and the peace of mind of a managed service. For a small site, replaceable, or simply install Plausible or Umami on your server.
perdez: Filtering of bots and junk traffic

kit.description: Email platform for creators: sign-up pages, newsletters, sequences, digital product sales and paid subscriptions. Free plan up to 10,000 subscribers; Creator at $33 a month.

As the free plan goes up to 10,000 subscribers, the saving often does not justify switching.

toggl-track.description: Time tracking: one-click timer, reports per client and per project, billable rates. Free plan up to 3 users; Starter at $9 per user per month.

At €12.50 a month, the time spent maintaining all of that costs far more than the subscription. For invoicing alone a free tool exists; for everything else, no.

For sensitive data that must not leave your machine, it is a real option.

Integrated web search and file handling
The speed of a hosted service
Usage included in the plan with no machine to maintain

digitalocean.description: Cloud hosting provider: virtual servers (Droplets), managed databases, storage and app platform. The cheapest Droplet costs $4 a month (1 vCPU, 512 MiB of RAM, 10 GiB of SSD).
digitalocean.justification: A hosting provider rents hardware and network: it cannot be coded. What you can reduce is the dependence on a particular offer: a VPS at any provider runs the same applications, and a deployment tool such as Coolify makes switching easier. Compare prices and location (European data centers) before committing; at this level the choice is about price and region, not features.
perdez: Backups and snapshots in a few clicks
alternatives: German provider of cloud and dedicated servers at tight prices.

bubble.description: No-code platform for building web applications visually, with built-in database, hosting and workflows. Free plan to develop; the Starter plan costs $59 a month billed annually.
bubble.justification: With a code assistant, a simple application (forms, database, user accounts) can be written in code and hosted for a few euros, with no workload-unit pricing and no lock-in. What you lose: the visual editor, hosting and database managed by Bubble, and not having to maintain security and updates. The hardest part is not building but keeping the app running over time: decide whether you will really do that.
perdez: The visual editor with no code to maintain
Hosting, database and workflows managed in one place
Security and updates handled by the vendor

mailgun.description: Email sending API for developers: transactional and bulk messages with delivery tracking. Free plan with 100 emails a day; the Basic plan starts at $15 a month for 10,000 emails.
mailgun.justification: Sending an email is easy; getting it to the inbox is not. Deliverability depends on the reputation of sending addresses, authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), handling of bounces and complaints, and warming up an address, which a provider does across thousands of customers. You can host your own sender (Postal), but a new server often lands in spam. For a few transactional emails, a provider's free plan is usually the better choice.
perdez: The reputation of established sending addresses
alternatives: Self-hosted email delivery platform (MIT); you handle server reputation and deliverability yourself.

hostinger.description: Web hosting provider: shared hosting, WordPress hosting, VPS and domain names. The cheapest shared plan is advertised at €2.99 a month with a 48-month commitment, renewing at €9.99 a month (3 websites, 20 GB SSD, weekly backups).
hostinger.justification: Shared hosting is a rental of space on a server: it cannot be coded. For a static site, free hosts (Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages) cost nothing; for several sites or an application, a small VPS with Coolify is about the same price and gives you more control. Read the conditions carefully: the advertised price requires a long commitment and the renewal price is more than three times higher.
perdez: Managed shared hosting with no server to administer
A free domain for the first year

bitly.description: Link shortener and QR code generator with click analytics. Free plan limited to 5 links a month; the Core plan costs $10 a month (annual billing only) for 100 links, and a custom domain only comes with the Growth plan at $29 a month.
bitly.justification: A link shortener is a table of codes and a redirect: Shlink does it on your own domain, with click statistics, for the cost of a small server. For a handful of links, Bitly's limits (5 a month for free, custom domain only from $29) are more expensive than hosting yourself. What you lose: the polished analytics dashboard, the QR code and landing page generator, and an uptime guarantee: if your server goes down, all your short links go down with it.

An uptime guarantee: your short links keep working if you do not maintain a server

uptimerobot.description: Website and service availability monitoring with alerts. Free plan with 50 monitors checked every 5 minutes; the Solo plan costs €9 a month billed annually (€10 monthly) for checks every minute.
uptimerobot.justification: Uptime Kuma, free software, does the same job: checks every minute or less, alerts by email, Telegram or other channels, and a public status page. The one thing to keep in mind: a monitor hosted on the same server as the site it watches goes down with it. Run it on a different machine, a small separate VPS or a home server, and the replacement is complete for a few euros.

Checks from several locations around the world

surveymonkey.description: Online survey tool with templates and response analysis. The free plan is limited to 10 questions per survey; the Standard monthly plan costs €39 a month for 1,000 responses, with €0.10 for each additional response.
surveymonkey.justification: A short survey (a few questions, results in a table or a chart) is quick to build with an assistant and costs nothing to host. For occasional use, a free form tool such as Tally already goes further than SurveyMonkey's free plan. What you lose: the survey templates, advanced analysis (cross-tabulation, filters), and paid respondent panels. For a customer survey or event feedback, building your own is plenty.

Export and integrations ready to use

Open-source form builder (AGPL), self-hostable.

Appsmith and ToolJet, free software, also offer a visual editor if you prefer clicking to coding. What you lose: Retool's library of ready-made components and connectors, permissions and audit logging, and not having to maintain the tool yourself. For a small team with a few screens, it is a good trade.

eventbrite.description: Event ticketing and promotion platform. Creating free events costs nothing; for paid tickets, ticketing fees are charged to buyers by default, and the organizer can choose to absorb them.
eventbrite.justification: Selling tickets to your own audience is easy to rebuild: a page, Stripe and a QR code scanned at the door. What Eventbrite sells is two other things: the discovery of your event by people who do not know you, and handling of payments, refunds and fraud at scale. If your audience already comes from you (your newsletter, your community), a self-hosted ticketing tool is enough; if you count on being found, it is not.
perdez: Discovery of your event by people who do not know you
Payments, refunds and fraud protection at scale
Built-in email and social promotion tools

gitlab.description: Git hosting and DevSecOps platform: repositories, merge requests, built-in CI/CD, security scanning and package registry. Free plan with 400 compute minutes a month; the Premium plan costs $29 per user a month billed annually.
gitlab.justification: GitLab's core is itself free software, and Gitea gives you repositories, merge requests, issues and CI on a small server in an afternoon. For a solo developer or a small closed team, it is enough. What you lose: the integrated security scanning, the container and package registry, the compliance features and the compute minutes of a managed service. For an organization that needs those, the Premium plan has real value.

obat.description: Quote and invoicing software for French construction tradespeople, with a library of 30,000 construction works with prices and labor times, 300 quote templates and electronic signature. Plans from about €25 to €129 excl. VAT a month.
obat.justification: A quote template is easy to build. What makes Obat valuable is the data: a library of 30,000 works with rates and labor times that someone keeps up to date, plus construction-specific features (progress invoices, site tracking) and compliance with the e-invoicing reform, whose calendar should be checked on the official texts. Without that library you start from a blank page on every quote. For a tradesperson, the time saved on pricing is worth far more than the subscription.
perdez: The library of 30,000 works with up-to-date rates and labor times
Progress invoices and construction site tracking
alternatives: Free ERP and CRM (GPL): quotes, invoices, customers and products, self-hostable. Does not do online filing or ready-made bank synchronization.

abby.description: Invoicing and accounting tool for French freelancers: unlimited quotes and invoices, URSSAF contribution estimates, bank connection and electronic signature. Free Basic plan; paid plans from €9 a month (regular price, often discounted).
abby.justification: A free plan with unlimited invoices already covers the basic need, and there is nothing to rebuild at that price. For paid plans, the value is in what surrounds invoicing: URSSAF declarations, bank connection, reminders and compliance with the e-invoicing reform (calendar to check on the official texts). Building those yourself costs more time than the €9 a month. Replace it only for invoicing alone, with a free tool.
alternatives: Free ERP and CRM (GPL): quotes, invoices, customers and products, self-hostable. Does not do online filing or ready-made bank synchronization.

henrri.description: Free invoicing software from the company Rivalis: unlimited quotes, invoices and credit notes, payment tracking and reminders, bank reconciliation and online payment. Premium tiers (Henrri Pro, Expert and VIP+) exist for more specialized needs.
henrri.justification: The software is already free and unlimited, so there is little to gain by rebuilding it: you would only swap a free tool for time spent maintaining your own. The real question is dependence on a free service whose business model comes from its paid tiers. Keep your data exportable and revisit only if the tool changes its terms or does not keep up with the e-invoicing reform (calendar to check on the official texts).
perdez: A free tool that is maintained and kept compliant by the vendor
alternatives: Free ERP and CRM (GPL): quotes, invoices, customers and products, self-hostable. Does not do online filing or ready-made bank synchronization.

cal-com.justification: Cal.com is itself open source: the replacement is hosting it yourself. A small server with Docker, a database and access to your calendar is enough to offer booking pages without a per-user subscription. What you lose: managed hosting, updates, the connected-app marketplace kept working for you, and support. For one person or a very small team, self-hosting is an afternoon; the cost is maintenance and the reliability of calendar connections.

The simplest setup, with no server

The free plan already covers 1 million events a month, so replacing it is mainly worth it for privacy or to stay in control of the data. What you lose: funnel and retention analysis, cohorts, session replays and the speed of a managed analysis tool.
